subject: Written opinion poll
comment: Hi, I would like to express my extreme disinterest in city council receiving a 35% pay increase on top of their new $212000 salary. An increase that follows inflation would be more reasonable, but 35% is absurd. I've worked full time as a RN in salt lake county for 5 years and the most I've ever been given as a raise is 2% a year. Until city council actually solves SLC inflation and housing crisis then they do not deserve a raise. They are bought out and their greed has been their first interest before the publics. Kelsey Reynolds

subject: Sports Entertainment District Agreement Needs Additional Stipulations for a better Sports Entertainment District
comment: Dear Sen. McCay, Sen. Cullimore, Rep. Moss, Rep. Hawkins, and Mr. Pierpont, I'm writing to ask that you get a better deal for Utah's taxpayers and for Salt Lake City with the Sports entertainment district. The general idea of the Sports and Entertainment District could be great for SLC. I think keeping the Jazz and the Utah Hockey Club sound great. However, we know from many studies that cities don't often get a true benefit from this. So, let's make this better. It's a contract after all and SEG doesn't seem to have too many obligations here. I do not understand why you cannot stipulate more from SEG in the contract. They are getting $900M of our money yet they seem to have few obligations other than the current zoning in place. The following provisions need to be added to the contract: 1. Better metrics on free tickets to low income people. Not just 'various games' but all games. 2. Include a non-car transportation plan/Travel Demand Management program. The traffic study that was included is for cars only and is really unacceptably bad. There's no mention of TRAX, Bus, FrontRunner, Walking, Biking, or reducing parking (which thus incentivizes more sustainable transportation). Non-car transportation needs to be spelled out in the contract. SLC has a commitment to sustainability- this contract does not hold true to that. 3. NBA and NHL provisions are spelled out. What if we get a WNBA team, women's hockey, arena football, or other big time sport? There needs to be contingencies for this too. 4. Some sort of plan for the Salt Palace. Just giving SEG control of this seems like a bad plan. Stipulations are needed. 5. The low-income housing surcharge is great, but not tied to inflation or anything. Now it sounds like a good bit of money, but in 20 years? Not so much. Please tie this to inflation and cost of living index. 6. There's little in the agreement that I see about ensuring public access and right of way to spaces that are currently public. SLC made this mistake when they sold a block of Main Street years ago and this space is not 24/7 public space. Please don't repeat this mistake. Current public spaces need to be kept public 24/7. 7. There is no sustainability requirement. They really need to agree to higher building standards and alternative energy use (solar etc) as part of the construction process. SLC has had a commitment to sustainability- this contract does not hold true to that. 8. With the Olympics coming in 2034, it should be part of the contract that SLC can use the facilities for the Olympics at no cost for renting the facilities. 9. The plans show nothing about a bike path or bike lanes on 300 W to N. Temple. There's some vague mention of this, but no requirement. This needs to be part of the contract. 10. There's little mention of bike facilities on any of the other roads leading to the Entertainment District. Please include those. 11. The contract has nothing about requiring bike parking on the facilities. There is currently no bike parking at the Delta Center. Since the renovations would be just that, there would be no zoning requirement to add bike parking since it's not a new construction project. Please include this so that people can more easily get to the Arena in a sustainable fashion. 12. A requirement for a percentage of locally owned businesses in the Entertainment District. 13. No destruction of Abrvenal Hall. This should be a stipulation. Yes, I'm aware that this is an SLCo facility. 14. No heliport - this should be a stipulation. While there are no plans for one, this should be permanently off the table. 15. Not a strong enough contract that would prevent the teams from leaving. 16. There is only the possibility of 2 SLC run public events from May 1 to September 15. This is problematic since it's only about 1/3 of the year and thus misses out on events during other times that the city might want to promote. And, it does not include February which is when the Olympics would be here. Why not have this be one per month for the entire year? These are just a few of the omissions that I found in a first reading of the contract. I'm sure that there are more, but these are glaring omissions and need to be corrected. We all want SLC to be vibrant, sustainable, and open. Please ensure this by updating the agreement. Thank you, Dave Iltis Salt Lake City resident Cycling Utah

subject: Raise???? | D1
comment: In these economic times where so many people are just trying to keep their head above water, you want a raise equivalent to most of your constituents yearly pay? For a part-time job? You should be ashamed! I guess that politics corrupts . I had hoped that it would have taken longer for you to go to the dark place you seem to be in. So I guess you have become a politician. Congratulations. I guess that you have adopted the phrase "Hurray for me and to hell with you"

subject: Release funding for foothill trails
comment: As a Salt Lake City resident who hikes and cycles the Foothills Trail system I urge you to release the funding now and finally resume development.

subject: Please resume the implementation of the foothill trail plan
comment: Dear Council, The implementation of the foothill trail master plan had been delayed long enough. Salt Lakers deserve a great trail system. I am frustrated by the delayed, which have been triggered by a small vocal minority to which the city has given disproportionate attention. Time to build the trails. Conducting studies after studies won't placate people who don't want trails in their backyard. Sincerely, Alessandro Rigolon

subject: Please expand SLC trails per the Master Plan!
comment: I would like to write in support of the expansion of the Foothill trail system and the implementation of the master plan. As a citizen who has lived in the Avenues from 2006 until recently, the expansion of our trail system has been exciting and long overdue! The new trails are fantastic, and I have been enjoying them immensely with my kids. Salt Lake has world-class recreation, but it hasn't had a world-class trail system to match. Now it can! I am concerned that a small vociferous minority may be successful in continuing to halt further trail development. I can personally attest that these trails are more popular than ever, and the new trails are a big reason for this. Sadly, the old trail system is not sustainable. Many trails went straight up hills and became terribly eroded over the years. In addition, (mostly) hikers made more and more unofficial, unsustainable "wildcat" trails that have multiplied as our population has grown. Having new separate biking and hiking trails has also diminished confrontations as well. And I feel that the main threat to our foothills is not a new network of trails—it's climate change. We need to keep our recreation local. People move to SLC for our world-class recreation. If we don't have a commensurate world-class trail network, people will continue to go elsewhere—the Cottonwoods, Draper, Park City—to seek out trails and emit tons of carbon dioxide as they drive to do so. As a SLC high-school mountain bike coach, I feel that we have to travel much further than need be to access suitable trails. It has been more discouraging to see trails continuing to expand in the foothills of North Salt Lake, Bountiful, Millcreek, and Draper but not in Salt Lake proper. Please continue the great work you all are doing and continue to expand our trails. I hope that you do not let a vocal minority dissuade you from doing so.

subject: Please provide funding for trails
comment: Please provide funding for trail expansion. I recreate in the foothills almost daily and I would love to see some new trails. I support creating separate hiking and mountain biking trails (especially creating downhill-only biking trails—this makes mountain biking safer for both for bikers and hikers). I would love to see an off-leash dog area, too.

subject: Raised Crosswalks
comment: Hi Dan, How would I go about recommending raised crosswalks on St. Mary's Way and Vista View Drive (84108) as shown in the picture? This is for traffic slowing and safer pedestrian crossings. Thanks, Laurel Hello Laurel, Thank you for your message. Our city transportation division manages requests like this. subject: CIP Grant- Harvey Milk Neighborhood Visibility
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Council Members, I am writing as the applicant for the Harvey Milk Neighborhood Visibility CIP Grant Proposal. We appreciate the support of the council on this project and realize that our project is large in scope with many considerations. As I mentioned when I attended your council meeting last month, we realize it may not be possible to fund everything on our wish list but ask for your support as budget allows to partially fund our project. As a reminder, below is a breakdown of the budget for our request. I would highlight the first two items, as our priorities for the project, and what we feel will have the most immediate impact to provide visibility for our community, and where we have some sources of outside funding to help, placing banners on the arms/poles, if provided by the CIP. Salt Lake City encourages and welcomes all residents and visitors to embrace our LGBTQ+ Community with equality and unity and provide a place to enjoy life and live and work in peace, safety, and love. Providing additional visibility creates a crucial sense of individual belonging and security for LGBTQ+ people. It is also important to show tourists and visitors that Salt Lake City, is a vibrant diverse community and a wonderful place to visit and live. In our current political environment, it is even more critical that we recognize and provide visibility to our marginalized communities and represent our city as a safe and welcoming space for all people. subject: Foothills Plan Evaluation and Recommendations Report
comment: I am writing to encourage the Council to remove the existing hold on the trail construction funding. I use the Foothill Trail system multiple times a week biking, hiking and trail-running by myself and with my kids. We love the new trails at Parley's Point. Improving and expanding the trail system is important for making it easy for all residents and especially the kids to get out and enjoy nature. For our kids: -More time on trails means less time in front of screens; -More time on trails means healthier kids, both physically and mentally. -More time on trails builds a love of nature and a desire to preserve our natural resources for the future. Please remove the hold and move forward without delay.

subject: Vision Zero City
comment: Dear Mayor Mendenhall, Your kind attention regarding the attached letter from the membership of Sweet Streets is greatly appreciated. Kind regards, Eric Kraan Sweet Streets, Board Member. cc: SL City Council.

subject: BST and Foothill Trails
comment: I understand there was a pause on implementing and building additional trails in our foothills. I am in full support of trail construction funding should be released, allowing Public Lands to continue implementing the Foothills Trail System Plan. I know this plan is already in place and needs to be implemented, but I just want to say that I am supportive of multi user trail systems that allow multi use and multi directional trails with the addition of uphill only and downhill only routes for mountain bikers. Granted that the downhill only trails are for bikes only and the uphill routes are multi-use. Thank you for supporting and being aggressive about creating new trails in our foothills which are a huge benefit to all in the Salt Lake Valley and connecting counties. Sincerely, Kevin Pferdner

subject: Council decision on planning commission's recommendation
comment: Dan, I may have missed this in your newsletter, so excuse me. Has the council made a decision on the rezoning request that was unanimously rejected by the planning commission and forwarded to council? The condo coalition is in the process of planning our next meeting. This topic was raised by several of the condos. Thanks so much! Martha Wunderli President | Management Committee Canyon Crest Homeowners Association

subject: CIP Application Funding
comment: Hello Councilmember Dugan, My name is Marcus Wright, a SLC and Central Ninth / Ball Park neighborhood resident, and I am writing to you to ask and encourage you to support funding for two CIP applications that I think would be a good investment for the city and have a broad positive impact on their communities. The first is the Fayette Avenue Street Improvements. This is an innovative project that is badly needed to improve Fayette Avenue and make it usable. Living near this stretch of road I can attest to how chaotic and unsafe it feels to traverse this street on foot or bike, which is a major artery in the neighborhood for all types of traffic. There is no sidewalk or lighting in the area, which makes walking down the street feel like the only option. There is underutilized land on the street that this project takes advantage of and upgrades, it also completes upgrades that have already been partially completed on the street and creates block long continuity with sidewalks and lighting. With hundreds of new apartments, residents, business and investments in the Central Ninth and Ballpark neighborhoods, this project is the perfect opportunity for the city to also invest and support this neighborhood, existing residents, and innovative zoning. The second project is Harvey Milk Boulevard Visibility. 900 South named after Harvey Milk is the perfect location to publicly support and highlight our City's vast LGBTQ+ community. This seems especially important with hostile national politics and local incidents of pride flags being vandalized within a block of 900 South. I would love to see the city step up in this way! I also believe this complements the brand new 9 Line trail and would be a boon and draw to business of all sorts along the street. Please consider funding in any way possible. Thank you for your time, Marcus Wright

subject: Please continue with the Foothills Trail System Master Plan!
comment: I am an Avenues resident that regularly uses the trails that have been completed to date under the Foothills Trail System Master Plan. They are a huge asset and have held up incredibly well over the past few years - in other words the concerns expressed about the "construction methods" of these trails appear to be completely unfounded. The full Foothills Trail System Master Plan has been held up for 3+ years by a vocal, anti-progress minority of Avenues residents. It is frankly disappointing that the Council bought into idea that we needed to "Save Our Foothills" when exactly what they needed saving from was never clear to me (and many of my neighbors). To me, the resistance to the Plan was NIMBYism, plain and simple. As time has gone, not having a comprehensive plan has done more harm than good as users continue to use social trails, including some mostly completed trails in the Plan (at the top of Dry Creek for example). It is time to move forward with the Foothills Trail System Master Plan and continue building a world class trail system right in the heart of our city!

subject: In Support of Trail Development
comment: Please accept this message in support of trail development in the Foothills. One of the key components of the master plan, that I believe is integral to accessibility and usability of the Foothills Trail System is the development of trails and specifically, the development of use-specific trails. While I understand that there are concerns about building downhill bike trails, and how that impacts hiking users of the trail system, I believe strongly that the development of downhill only trails is integral to the future development of this area. As is the case at many nearby recreation areas (Corner Canyon and Park City, for example) having downhill only bike trails increases the safety and accessibility of all users. The foothills area is used extensively by both cyclists and hikers. While hikers may be uncomfortable with being told they cannot use a downhill mountain biking trail, to neglect the benefits of downhill only trails is to neglect that cyclists regularly use this area. Since cycling has been, and will continue to be, a significant use of this area, I believe that the best way forward is to acknowledge that and plan accordingly. Furthermore, the population of Salt Lake City is growing quickly, with one of the large appeals to many moving to the area is the accessibility of outdoor pursuits to the city. Expanding the trail system will increase this access and provide greater good to a greater number of users. I understand the concerns from residents of the area that the trails they know are changing, however I am concerned that these objections are made by a small group of people whose concerns are narrow in scope, failing to understand the value of public lands to the more general public. While demands for more thorough environmental impact assessments may appear to be well-meaning, I believe this is a tactic may simply be used to delay the project or reduce its feasibility.

subject: Implementation of Foothills Trails System Plan
comment: Kudos to the Department of Public Lands for doing the necessary due diligence concerning the assessment of Phase I and for developing a framework for next steps. I encourage the council to remove the pause on funding so that Public Lands can move forward with the much-needed trail construction. I also look forward to learning more about increased opportunities for public engagement with the planning and maintenance of trails.

subject: Please Continue expanding Foothill trail system
comment: I purchased my home on Terrace Hills in January 2018. A big part of why we choose to purchase this home was due to the trail network in the area. My family loves hiking, walking our dog, running and mountain biking on these trails. We would very much love the trails and would like to continue to see them further developed. We also very much enjoyed the dedicated trail designations to keep mountain bikes on and off certain trails to improve safety along with the updated signage. Though I would like to see more permeate signage as there are people that love to rip the signs out for whatever reason. It would also be nice if our trail system would update the trail etiquette right of way that other states have been adopting successfully, where all downhill traffic needs to yield to all uphill traffic. It's a very simple and safe way for all trail users to use the trails and be respectful to each other. Lastly, as I'm getting older the class 1 e bikes are becoming more desirable as a mode of using the trails. Class 1 e bikes are no more dangerous than regular mountain bikes, as they are pedal assist only. If you're not pedaling, you're not moving and at the end of the day it's more about faster cadence to climb through challenging trail conditions than speed. The class 2 & 3 with their throttles do pose more danger as users can accelerate quickly without effort and should not be allowed. Thank you for your time and consideration.

subject: recommendations for the Foothill Trails
comment: Yes, release the funding to build more trails. I use the trails multiple times a week, the current trails are well used more are needed to further disperse the traffic. The most recent trails are great, it would be nice to see more hiking and mtb specific trails added to the system.

subject: Please remove the hold on the foothill trail system development
comment: As a long time SLC resident and outdoor lover, I urge you to continue the development of the Foothill Trail System. Other trail systems (Draper, Midler, Farmington, etc.) are proof that these are valuable additions to our community. Please continue developing and funding new trails in the SLC foothills.

subject: SLC Foothills Master Plans
comment: Hello, I have been following the SLC Foothills Master Plan since 2015 and I was really excited when the City started working on expanded and improving the much needed trail network. Although there have been some improvements since they were put on hold, I think it would add so much value to the community to move forward with the plan. I recreate in the SLC trails 3-4 days a week and every fall/spring it becomes dangerous with the volume of trail users. We need to increase the capacity of these trails to match the growth of the city. Please build more trails. Sincerely, Ryan O'Mahony (Avid Hiker and Biker)

subject: Foothills Plan Evaluation and Recommendations Report
comment: I would like to encourage the Council to remove the existing hold on trail construction funding. I am a 40-year resident of SLC and very regular user of the system as a mountain biker, hiker and trail runner, both on my own and with family. We have loved the expansions that are in place including 19th Ave, the Avenues Ridge, Parley's Point and the Grandeur Peak to Pipeline extension. Certainly, separating downhill bike traffic makes it more fun for all users. I feel like the original plan, while perhaps needing minor adjustments and optimization, was well thought-out and will ultimately be a major boon for the community. I do hope there are provisions included to help enforce the dog-leashing rules that are already in place (but which are universally violated). Nothing interrupts a great trail flow more readily or more often than even a well-meaning and well-behaved dog blocking the trail and investigating other users.

subject: Support for Moving SLC Foothill Trails System projects and funding forward
comment: I noticed that the the Council is taking a straw poll at its meeting next week on whether to release the hold on construction funding for projects in the SLC Foothills Trail System Plan. Please take any action to move forward trail construction and maintenance. "Yes in our backyard.", we've waited long enough. The Plan represents a great opportunity to make much needed improvements and additions to our cherished city trails resource that accessible without requiring a long drive. The trails investment will pay dividends for generations -- children, adults, seniors who hike, bike, dog walk, and otherwise enjoy appreciating, connecting, and unwinding together in the context of our natural surroundings -- and for generations to come.

subject: continuing delays in trail construction constitute a safety hazard
comment: I regularly use the shoreline trail system between North Salt Lake and Dry Creek Canyon canyon by mountain bike. I am always respectful to other trail users and give the right-of-way to hikers and runners. We have been promised trail improvements since 2020 and the City Council has failed to deliver on this promise. The current plan includes useful tasks that should have been completed years ago. In it's current form, the Shoreline Trail system is a safety hazard. I have been bitten twice (Morris Meadows and Dry Creek) and chased once by an off-leash dog (Morris Meadows). My impressions are that people on mountain bikes can be threatening to dogs and that they act in ways to protect their humans. There are no signs indicating that dogs are required to be on leash. These instances would have been avoided if trails separating hikers/dog walkers and bikers were in place. I recommend prohibiting dogs on the shoreline trail until new trails are constructed and improving signage to include the requirement for dogs to be leashed. Thank you for your consideration.

subject: Foothills Trails
comment: To a degree, inclusivity seems to have fallen out of favor nationally. It has not in the National Interscholastic Cycling Association. Many schools around Salt Lake City and County use the Salt Lake City foothills trail to bring children who may otherwise be excluded from many social and sporting activities to a Jr. High and High School club. In recently years, we have seen an escalation of conflicts between various types of trail users and feel strongly that dedicated trails (such as those which were planned) will help alleviate this stress. No longer can nearby residents claim the Foothills trails as their own backyard. The Bonneville Shoreline Trail system must be expanded to include a greater number of trail users while working to avoid conflict between hikers, bikers, runners, dog walkers, and other lovers of the outdoors. As a former Salt Lake City resident, current Salt Lake County resident, trail user, high school mountain bike coach, and longtime BST trail user, I URGE the Salt Lake City Council to release the funds set aside for the proper development of Salt Lake City Trail systems.

subject: Expand Foothill Trails!
comment: We need to expand the Foothill trails! They are incredible trails and it is such a shame that they were preciously shutdown/expansion.

subject: foothill plan evaluation and recommendations report
comment: It's time to release the funding for the trails project. This shouldn't have been delayed. Population is growing, people are in the foothills and more are coming. Have sustainable trails is the only option. It's also what is best for the health of the community. Let's make it happen. Don't let a vocal few outweigh what is needed for our city.

subject: Foothills trail system plan
comment: I am writing concerning the Foothills Trail Project. I am a 28 year resident of the Avenues who has recreated (hiking, mountain biking) in the Foothills since 1995. I can remember the area before there was a Bonneville Shoreline Trail and I recreate on the new trails that were constructed several years ago. It is my understanding that the Salt Lake City Council will be presented with findings and recommendations from the Department of Public Lands at a work session on Aug 27. It is also my understanding that there will be a straw poll at the meeting to determine if the construction funding should be released, allowing public Lands to continue implementing the Foothills Trail System Plan. I am writing to express my strong support for the release of funds to continue construction of the Foothills Trail System Plan. The new trails added a few years ago have proven enormously popular. As a hiker and a mountain biker, I appreciate the segregation of user groups for many trail segments. It is a tremendous resource for the community with recreational users spanning all age groups and should be completed as soon as possible. Sincerely, Jim Steenburgh

subject: Foothills Trail Plan funding release
comment: To the SLC Council: Thank you so much for prioritizing trails and outdoor recreation in your budget. I use trails most of the year and generally use them about 5 times per week. I have absolutely loved the new trails that were built a couple of years ago. I mountain bike, run, and hike alone and with friends. I love being able to access a variety of trails without having to drive up a canyon or just having a very short drive. I have watched the process with the consultants and am pleased with what they've done to point out best practices in terms of trail alignments, directional trails, signage, trailheads, etc. The responsible staff in the Parks Division has been responsive to constituents and worked hard to keep communication open and transparent. The fact that SLC is a landowner of foothill property is such a great opportunity to offer residents recreation immediately adjacent to their city. I hope you have been able to enjoy the new trails and will vote today to release the funding to continue the new trail construction.

subject: Foothill bike trail expansion
comment: I am reaching out as a member of the bike community to ask that we please try and push through to make these plans happen. I have been riding these trails my whole life and each new one makes such a difference. Thanks Benjamin Bigwood

subject: Foothills trail system plan
comment: Release the funds and start building trails ASAP!

subject: SLC trails
comment: Hello Council members and to whom it may concern, As a resident of Salt Lake City's Avenues neighborhood for over 30 years. I need to tell you how important the trails system in the foothills is to my family, my quality of life and the community of this city. We use the trails all the time. Not a week goes by when one of us is not by foot, with our dog, or by bike, using those trails. After all of these years of use, and seeing the spiderwebbing of extra trails and the erosion it caused, I was thrilled when the master plan was developed and was started to be implemented in 2020. I was very disappointed when a few people with reactionary, unrealistic views of the trail system made some noise and the plan was paused. The growth in the number of people using the trail system is huge and that will continue to grow into the future. Without the full implementation of the trail master plan, development and implementation of future master plans and full signage and enforcement, ecological damage is being done, conflicts are arising on the trails and traffic is being concentrated in certain areas. Developed trails are a benefit for all residents of Salt Lake. Establishing designated trails for bikes, dogs and hikers within a multi use system reduces conflict and enhances enjoyment, and quality of life. (19th avenue bike trail is excellent!) I urge you to release the pause, finish the master plan and continue budgeting for planning and development of the trail system into the future. Sincerely Ezra Thomas Jones

subject: Foothill Trail System Plan
comment: Dear Chris and Council, I am an Avenues resident writing in support of resuming the Foothill Trails System. I am a regular trail user, both by bike and foot. While Phase 1 may have had some minor issues, it was a huge step in the right direction by separating users and creating both pedestrian-only and downhill-only trails. Despite complaints, it seems the number of new trail miles built for each user were equitable. Clearly some of the loudest opposition voices came from Upper Avenues residents who are frustrated by cars parked on their street. That problem isn't going away by stalling the expansion plan. One way to alleviate this would be to invest in more trailheads and designated parking. In terms of trail expansion, it's critical. The growth in the city isn't slowing down. People move to Salt Lake City for the rare combination of urban life and easy outdoor access. Trying to stifle trail use by shutting down trail construction is simply short-sighted. Hikers and bikers are going to use the system regardless, but the status quo is only creating trail congestion and increased conflict. Look at cities that are building great in-town trail networks — Boise, Duluth, Ketchum, even Draper! They've embraced expansion to spread out users all while doing so with minimal impact on the environment. Salt Lake City has the perfect opportunity to expand its reputation as a dynamic, thriving city with second-to-none outdoor recreation opportunities. But the current trail system isn't keeping pace with the city's needs. Let's move forward and get some shovels in the dirt! Best, Michael Yount -- Michael Yount

subject: Foothills Trail Plan
comment: Please release funds so that building can resume on the Foothill Trail system. The delay has been far too long. I understand some people (a vocal minority) had concerns with the previous trail-building. But I think those concerns can be addressed, and it has taken far too long to do so. Did you know the Manhattan Project needed 3 years to build the first atomic bomb? How can it take 4 years to figure out where and how to build some hiking and mountain biking trails? -Rob Scott

subject: Foothill Trail Improvement/Construction
comment: Hello, My name is Grant Hulsberg from Millcreek Utah and I'm reaching out about the upcoming vote on August 27th regarding the Foothill trail improvement projects. I'm a member of both the Skyline High Mountain Bike team and the Maybird cycling team which are both teams based right here in Salt Lake City. I spend a lot of time on my bike training and practicing my skills in order to be the best racer that I can be. The trails that I ride have helped me become not only a better athlete but have increased my quality of living and made me fall in love with all that the Salt Lake Valley has to offer. The saddest part about all of this is how far behind Salt Lake City is compared to other cities like Draper or Park City. In terms of how many trails are made compared to how much potential there is Salt Lake City is doing very poorly. I would love to have more trails closer to home so that I could ride my bike from my house and explore the beautiful mountains around us. This is why I believe that the Foothill Trail Improvement project is necessary to further develop the recreational facilities in Salt Lake City. Thank you for your time. Grant Hulsberg

subject: Foothills Plan Evaluation and Recommendations Report
comment: Please remove the existing hold on trail construction funding. I use the foothill trails every week both to bike and hike or run. Some of the new trails that were added a few years ago are wonderful and have eased the congestion a little. We need so much more. It isn't fun for anyone when hikers and bikers and dogs try to use just a few wonderful trails. More trails and more use separation is badly needed. I would be happy to talk more about this or to support this effort in any way I can.

subject: foothills trail system master plan - move forward
comment: The master plan has been halted long enough, move forward with it. More trails is never a bad thing, it's already been approved and worked with and has already garnered lots of positive feedback. It would be amazing to see it come to fruition.

subject: More well built trails, dispersed parking and great communication benefit all and in fact actually save the foothills
comment: In an effort to safe the foothills, the organization, save our foothills, has helped to destroy them. In the few years that the new trails have gone in those trails have helped to disperse traffic, separate user groups and create pathways for people that limit user erosion. In that short time the at first unsightly trails have grown in and become hidden trails through the foothills. Yes, there were some growing pains. And probably these growing pains were largely due to communication and the quality and placement of trails. Unfortunately this gave save-our-foothills a foothold to stop all progress. And so going forward, and forward we should go, these things must be handled more professionally - both the construction and the communication. Missteps aside, the benefits of new trails for all user groups is incredible and honestly undeniable. Just the downhill only mountain bike trails alone have lessened dangerous situations and uncomfortable interactions. More trails that separate bikers and hikers will have be even better for both groups, and, when done correctly create trails that people will travel to experience - which of course brings us to the next question which is parking - creating many dispersed, small parking areas which starts people at many different trailheads is a great way to both spread people out on the trails as well as get them parking in many different areas. We need more trails for more people for more user groups spread out across a greater area - this is what we started doing. We need to communicate well. And we need to move forward on this and not languish because a few people wish it was still 1980. There are a lot more people getting out and that is a good thing. The more people who enjoy the outdoors the more people will support outdoor initiatives and efforts to protect nature and our environment. And we can do this in a way that serves a bigger community while preserving our natural areas, protecting our heritage and environment. In fact, if we do not take these steps more and more illegal and erosion prone trails will pop up, more people will roam off trail, more people will have dangerous run-ins. Forward on well crafted trail building! Thank you, Pete

subject: Resume Foothills Trail
comment: Hello, One of the greatest draws to Salt Lake City is how close outdoor access is to an urban environment. As our population continues to grow and thrive so must our infrastructure, trails and outdoor access included. The trails added in 2020/21 added increased options for both hikers and bikers alike. Downhill only mountain bike trails offer improved safety for both hikers and bikers as they significantly decrease risk of collisions. Please consider resuming the Foothills Trail projects as they greatly benefit our community. Thank you, Armando Tirado

subject: concern over planning
comment: I welcome the chance to provide my input. However, I have to wonder why I should expect that you will pay attention to the opinions of people such as myself (who are admittedly not expert urban planners) since you are seeming to more or less ignore the opinion of the Planning Commission who are, hopefully, experts? You are asking all of us, including those who will never attend a basketball or hockey game to pay increased sales tax, and giving this billionaire developer what amounts to carte blanche with very little oversight, especially regarding building height. It gives the impression that you are just going through the formality of asking for feedback before you just go ahead and do whatever it is that you were going to do anyway, In this era of identifying populations whose voices are not heard, those of us who come downtown for the symphony, opera, ballet, UMOCA, movies and dining, but not sports, are feeling that we are falling in that category of being ignored and not represented.

subject: Please don't let the NIMBY's ruin it for the whole city.
comment: The foothill master plan was thorough and comprehensive. The only reason construction stopped is because the very wealthy few whose houses border the area don't like sharing the public land they like to think of as their back yard. Please don't continue punishing the majority of your constituents just to appease a handful of cranky people.

subject: Foothills Plan Evaluation
comment: Please remove the hold on funding trail improvement and maintenance. Our Foothill trails are an invaluable resource. The Foothill trails give Salt Lake residents the opportunity to recreate and relax in nature close to home. Please allow work to resume on the Foothill trails master plan. We all benefit from improvements to trails.

subject: Let's continue to grow and evolve the trail systems
comment: The hills and mountains above the city should be more accessible to residents. Activities like biking, e-biking, adaptive biking, hiking, and trail running contribute to a healthy and happy community. Let's encourage these by expanding our trail systems.

subject: Foothills trail expansion
comment: Hello! Just want to comment that I support expanding the trail network in the foothills. I live a few miles away so I can easily mountain bike in the foothills, without even driving to the trailhead. More trails would get me out on my bike more often, and I'm sure that's true for a lot of people. The world is better if more people are out using the trail system should definitely be expanded!

subject: Support expanding the trail network
comment: I just wanted to write to say I hope the mountain bike trail expansion will continue in the Foothills. We moved to Salt Lake and love the great mountains around the city. Having trails in the Foothills area for mountain biking is a huge draw to the city and elevates living in Salt Lake above other places. The trails that have gone in are excellent and expansion would provide more variety and open up outdoor access to more people. It would be great to look into riding near Salt Lake and not have to drive far to get to trails. Having more high quality trails close to the city will be a huge benefit to the community. Thank you.

subject: We need more mountain bike trails
comment: We don't have enough mountain biking trails in the Salt Lake Valley. My 2 children ride on the Skyline High School Mountain Bike Team and there aren't enough trails for them or for the high school teams ride. Please invest in creating more trails and maintenance of existing trails. Thanks!!!

subject: Supporting new trail development in the foothills
comment: Hi, I heard you all are hearing the results of the Dept of Public Lands' study on the foothills trails plan. As a SL resident of Salt Lake and avid mountain biker and trail runner, I wanted to write to express my support for this plan and for new trail construction in general. Salt Lake is a hub for outdoors enthusiasts and particularly mountain bikers, which you can see any day at almost any trailhead in SLC. Currently, there are far too few trails to match demand, which encourages environmentally-destructive hiking and biking off-trail. Furthermore, excessive demand leads to overcrowding and user conflict on the existing trails. The Foothills Trails Plan provides a great fix to all of these problems, providing much-needed new trail construction in our beautiful foothills. I've ridden 19th ave, the first of the new trails, quite a lot, and it's an amazing bike trail that's fun for both beginner and advanced riders. Don't yield to NIMBYs who don't know anything about trail construction or impacts!! To preserve the Foothills for future generations, please implement the Foothills Trails Plan in its entirety. The outdoors enthusiasts of Salt Lake will thank you (and the outdoors themselves would if they could!).

subject: Foothill trails need expansion
comment: Deer Valley and Park City's development of mountain biking and hiking trails has increased business in the summer dramatically. There are some great trails in the foothills but there aren't enough. Trails are overcrowded, and because the selection is slim, riders are choosing other locations. Lost lad and bobsled are a great start, add some more and you'll bring riders and their business to the area.

subject: Foothills Master Plan
comment: Salt Lake City Council, I understand you'll be reviewing the Foothills Master Plan soon. I love mountain biking, hiking, backpacking, and other recreational activities. Salt Lake City has unparalleled access to mountain recreation, but as our population has grown and the popularity of outdoor activities has increased, Salt Lake City needs to do more. Salt Lake City has lagged behind Draper, Lehi, Herriman and Spanish Fork in developing new trails and promoting outdoor recreation. The other Cities have benefited substantially by investing in new trails and promoting healthy outdoor activities. the trails around SLC are at capacity, and user conflicts are increasing. The City needs many more Mountain Bike specific trails. Mountain biking has experienced exponential growth over the last 3 years and we need more trails to properly enjoy our foothills. I am writing to voice my support for the Foothills Master Plan. The newly completed trails in the Foothills are fantastic, and I'd love to see phase 1 completed and phase 2 begun on schedule. Please don't heed to the loud minority who hate mountain bikers and want to stop the creation of more trails. I appreciate your consideration. Sincerely, Brian Samuel

subject: Development of more Mtn biking/hiking trails
comment: Salt Lake City Council, I have read that you are going to review the Foothills Master Plan soon. I love mountain biking, hiking, backpacking, and other recreational activities. Salt Lake City has unparalleled access to mountain recreation, but as our population has grown and the popularity of outdoor activities has increased, Salt Lake City needs to do more.
