I am writing to voice my support for the Foothills Master Plan. The newly completed trails in the Foothills are fantastic, and I'd love to see phase 1 completed and phase 2 begun on schedule. Please don't heed to the loud minority who hate mountain bikers and want to stop the creation of more trails. I appreciate your consideration. Thank you, Lari Todd

subject: Support moving forward with the foothill trails
comment: I support that the SL Council will vote YES to release the funds to implement the foothill construction and allow public lands to implement the Foothill Trails System plan. The plan is necessary for Salt Lake residents to enjoy our open space and public lands.

subject: Vote yes to release city funding for foothill trails
comment: Mountain biking has exploded in popularity and the need for purpose built and directional trails is necessary for safety and recreation of residents. Please vote yes to release the funding.

subject: Support more Foothill Trails
comment: I was pretty sad when I heard in the past that the new Foothill Trails were being delayed or possibly even cancelled. I heard recently though that you'll be reviewing the Foothills Master Plan for upcoming phases! I just wanted to voice my support in increasing the amount of trails in the area. While I understand not all trails can be used for all users I think we can all agree that more trails allows for more spread out use of the trails and therefore are even more enjoyable time. I have loved seeing the growth of trails in Draper, Park City, Herriman, and other cities. I believe more trails will bring more people into the area which will also have positive economic impact. Maybe that can help us fund the new Utah Hockey Team Delta Center upgrades as well. Thanks for your time, Tanton Jeppson

subject: Foothills Master Trail Plan
comment: Hello. I am a regular user of the foothills trail system. I participated in the original master plan information collection and feedback as advertised by the city on signage along the trails and was extremely disappointed when the process was halted. I think the surprise from certain individuals about the trail building demonstrates their lack of use and attention to these trails. As a regular user I very much appreciate the interest in reducing user conflict by designating certain trails for hiking and others for biking. I hope the city will pick this project back up to improve the area for all those who actually frequent the area.

subject: More Trails Now!
comment: Please fund trails! I now drive to areas adding to congestion and pollution. My friends, who can afford to live in our city, are being attracted and choosing to live closer to established trails. I would use new foothills trails weekly to commute and exercise. My interaction with both bikers and hikers is always positive but current trails are getting crowded and dangerous. My family supports better signage - please warn innocent hikers (some with dogs) of Bobsled danger or serious injury will occur. My family supports the balanced trail system previously outlined. We want a directional Dry Creek to solve that now dangerous bottleneck. We want better access to Mt. Wire and Mt. Van Cott. I believe trails draw genuine investment to our city. I really enjoyed the few new trails built but they now need some maintenance. There is so much potential in our foothills! Please fund and prioritize more trails now.

subject: Foothills plan Evaluation and Recommendations report
comment: I would like to encourage the council to remove the existing hold on planning of the Foothills trail system. I use the trails with my family multiple times a week. It has been so nice to stay close to home and be able to ride to the trails from our house. I ride the Park City trails frequently and often get asked what my favorite trails are in SLC and I tell them Park City. I have enjoyed the new Parley's Point trail and my son even rode all the way to Rattle Snake. Please continue moving forward so we can recreate in our own communities more! Thank you!

subject: Foothill trails
comment: This would improve our city tremendously. We are and have not been great about creating recreational opportunities with in our city for public access. We need more biking options off road and bike lanes as well as hiking access for our children to be able to get out and enjoy nature and to learn to love it the way we do. I would ask that you consider this and vote for this and it enhances the lives of many.

subject: more trails are good for salt lake city
comment: I am a Salt Lake City resident, working at the University of Utah and volunteering as a high school mountain biking coach for the Salt Lake Center for Science Education, a Title 1 public charter high school in Rose Park. As a native Utahn, I strongly believe that expanding the network of trails in the foothills surrounding Salt Lake City will greatly benefit those living in the Salt Lake Valley. These trails provide accessible and enjoyable opportunities for walking, mountain biking, hiking, and even dog walking, encouraging residents to engage in regular physical activity. Consistent exercise is crucial for maintaining a healthy body, improving cardiovascular health, and building strength and endurance. In addition to the physical benefits, spending time on these trails has a profound impact on mental and emotional health. Immersing oneself in nature helps reduce stress, anxiety, and depression. Connecting with nature allows people to unplug from daily demands, offering a mental reset that improves mood and mental clarity. Furthermore, these trails enhance our appreciation for Utah's natural beauty. The panoramic views and seasonal changes in the landscape inspire a sense of wonder and gratitude. This connection to nature fosters a greater sense of stewardship for the environment, particularly among young people, encouraging them to protect and preserve the natural spaces that contribute so much to their well-being. Park City has become world-renowned for its trail system, featuring purpose-built and directional trails that keep users safe and dispersed. Our high school team often drives to Park City to ride because our local trails are so crowded. However, it's not environmentally sustainable for us to drive to Park City twice a week. We would love to see the city government prioritize expanding and improving the local trail system to make it safer, larger, and more accessible, reducing overcrowding and benefiting the entire community. Thank you, Traci

subject: Foothill Masterplan
comment: We need to build the new trails proposed in the approved trail plan. SLC trails are often crowded. More trails will meet the growing demand and ensure positive outdoor experiences.

subject: Foothills Master Plan
comment: I'm writing in support of removing the hold on the Foothills Master Plan. I'm a Salt Lake City resident and frequent user of the SLC foothills trails. The proposed master plan is a significant improvement of the current system and will allow greater enjoyment of this natural amenity while minimizing impact.

subject: 8/27 council vote
comment: PLEASE do as you promised so many years ago and complete all the phases of the Foothill Trail System Plan. I have been patiently waiting for more trails for 20+ years of the 30 years I have been using them. The trails are only being more utilized (which is such a benefit to all – psychologically, physically, socially, etc) and more trails are desperately needed! Please don't let a small minority of old, vocal, NIMBY too much time on their hands- ruin it for the rest of us. We have been patient during this pause, but it was promised as that, A PAUSE. I (and countless others) utilize all the new trails for a mixture of mountain biking, hiking and trail running and they are delightful and provide me with options that I truly appreciate. I love living in the Avenues and leaving directly from my house to enjoy the trail system, like so many of my neighbors. Let's get this job done!!

subject: Release funding for trails in salt lake city
comment: I understand the council is considering releasing funding to continue to build out foothill trails that were approved several years ago. I believe this should be done. As it is residents of Salt Lake City often have to travel to other cities to take advantage of the trails they have built. As the premier city in Utah, Salt Lake City should be the leader in recreation trails for its citizens, we have ceded this to Draper, Bluffdale, Herriman, North Salt Lake, etc. let's do right for our citizens and approve this funding without delay.

subject: More, Better SLC Foothills Trails Now
comment: The new trails above Morris Meadows have been wonderful and after a couple years are no longer even visible. The NIMBYism of the Avenues needs to go away. The city is growing, the hikery biker issue isn't getting better only worse and the new trails already make a difference. I strongly support moving forward with the master plan as decided. I use the trails daily for dog walks, big hikes, and bikes. The new trails are great, but could use the maintenance they haven't seen the last couple of years The master plan is a great balance All SLC foothills trails are crowded, more please!

subject: Foothill trail expansion
comment: I just wanted to emphasize this trail system for the benefit of our community. Specifically, if you look at the numbers of youth who are on bikes and enjoying outdoors to relieve both mental and physical stress, you appreciate the importance of having access to such trail systems. Hundreds of kids take part in trail maintenance volunteer programs to show the support for areas they like to ride.

subject: Foothill Trails Master Plan Comment
comment: As a long-time Salt Lake resident, I am excited to hear that the Council is re-prioritizing trails in the Foothills. I use the Foothill trails weekly for mountain biking and trail running with my dog. I support investment in new trails, trail maintenance, conflict prevention design, signage, and trailheads. The valley is growing and our Foothill trails recreation opportunities should also increase to help provide accessible outdoor recreation without the need to drive to a canyon to do so.

subject: We need more trails for all user types
comment: I'm happy to hear that the SLC Council is re-prioritizing funding for trails again. I have been a SLC resident for 23 years. I use the trails for biking and hiking with my dogs. We need more trails options that are closer to home to support our growing population. I strongly support building more trails and improving the trails we have. Along with my daughter that rides with NICA we are always happy to volunteer to do trail work to support our local trail builders.

subject: SLC Foothill Trails Comments
comment: Dear Council, I can only hope this is a sign of the reprioritization of trail construction and improvement. SLC MUST invigorate their trails construction and improvement. This is an issue for paramount importance to so many of your constituents. I have been deeply saddened to see this process get derailed for years, when the demand is high, the need is great, and the improvement to quality of life and outdoor culture is so needed. Please prioritize this and see that it happens on very short order. My family of 5 and our network of friends rely on trails to recreate, meditate, exercise, commune with others, and above all, appreciate the glorious outdoors SLC presents. I have been nothing but frustrated watching a select few derail a project that benefits so many. It is time to do the greatest good for the vast majority. Please execute the trails plan. It is really not that that complicated. With deep appreciation. Scott Martin

subject: Foothills trail system plan
comment: Salt Lake City Council, I understand you'll be reviewing the Foothills Master Plan soon. As an active outdoorsman and lifetime resident of Utah, my family and I love mountain biking, hiking, backpacking, and other recreational activities. Salt Lake City has unparalleled access to mountain recreation, but as our population has grown and the popularity of outdoor activities has increased, Salt Lake City needs to do more. Salt Lake City has lagged behind Draper, Lehi, Herriman and Spanish Fork in developing new trails and promoting outdoor recreation. The other Cities have benefited substantially by investing in new trails and promoting healthy outdoor activities. The trails around SLC are at capacity, and user conflicts are increasing. The City needs many more Mountain bike specific trails. Mountain biking has experienced exponential growth over the last 3 years and we need more trails to properly enjoy our foothills. Salt Lake City needs more trails, and I'm writing to voice my support for the Foothills Master Plan. The newly completed trails in the Foothills are fantastic, and I'd love to see phase 1 completed and phase 2 begun on schedule. Please don't heed to the loud minority who hate mountain bikers and have a N.I.M.B.Y. attitude and want to stop the creation of more trails. I appreciate your consideration, and thank you for your service! Jared K. Williams P.E.

subject: ABravanel hall
comment: Whatever your discussion and decisions might be—DO NOT MOVE ABRAVANEL HALL!!!. I cannot make the meeting but I would hope that you take my request seriously. Move the damn hockey gleacm before you move Abravanel hall. Do not cave in to the money of this mid town charlatan. Gene Gene Fitzgerald Emeritus Professor of Russian Lang., Lit., and Culture U. of Utah [redacted-email]

subject: Remove hold on trail construction
comment: Council Members, I am writing to encourage the Council to remove the existing hold on trail construction funding. I use the Foothill Trail system multiple times a week, biking, hiking, and walking my dog. The new trails have greatly improved the quality of life for residents of SLC, but the project wasn't completed due to lobbying by a group of misguided NIMBYs. Please rectify this by removing the hold on funding so new trails can be built. Lawrence Dunn Ph.D. [redacted-email]

subject: Foothills Trails
comment: Good Day, My name in Chris Donaldson. I am 69 years old and live in the Avenues and spend many hours hiking the foothills from Ensign Peak in the north to Neff's Canyon in the south. I am concerned about the release of the remaining $380,000 of funds earmarked for trails. Please do not release these funds to Public Lands without having specific plans to invest these funds for what they were intended. Specifically, I would request that you spend the funds for the following projects that have either not been started or have not been completed before releasing additional funds: • Scientific and user data studies • Foothills land use management plan • Trail maintenance plan and protocols • Trail signs, wayfinding maps, information signs • Formation of stakeholder engagement committee • Environmental impact statements The trails in the Foothills are a precious amenity to Salt Lake City and contribute significantly our quality of life and tourism. I often encounter hikers from out of state that have sought the trails as part of their visit. I really appreciate all that you do. Best Regards.

subject: Foothills Master Plan
comment: Hello! I love our SLC foothills and can't wait to see work resume to put the Foothills Master Plan into place. As a frequent user of the trails above the Avenues, I cherish the work already completed and am excited for further phases to roll out. There is one particular part of a frequent hike that I do where improvements have been on hold for several years to add a switchback to a very popular but badly eroded social trail that will make it usable in a way that today, is a pretty sketchy route down. Please approve the resumption of the work to complete the Foothills Master Plan! Many thanks for all you do, Steve

subject: More Mountain bike Trails
comment: Hello, I am the head coach of the Olympus High school mountain bike team. We have 120 kids on our team this year. We could really benefit from having more trails close to home. As it stands now, we break into about 10 groups and go to different trailheads in Park city, Draper, salt lake, bountiful. (Commuting 30-60 min). It would be a game changer to have more close "home trails" that we could commute by bike to the trailheads. I have been mountain biking for 25 years and it's been amazing to watch this sport grow. With the high school league as large as it is we need more trails to keep up with the growth. I would love to see something similar to the corner canyon trail system in our foothills. We teach our kids the importance of sharing and respecting trails with all users! With the amount of kids in the league that are required to do trail work, you would have free labor to build the whole system! Thanks!

subject: Foothill Trail Construction and Usage Etiquette/Enforcement
comment: As a foothill trail user, usually multiple days a week, primarily by bike, the area is immensely popular and the resumption of new trail construction and existing trail maintenance would be much appreciated! More trails will help spread crowds and the addition of more single use trails keeps things safer for hikers and bikers. The education and enforcement of dog leash rules is needed! Most dogs are off leash on the BST which is dangerous for bikers and disobedient dogs alike. Additionally, dogs off leash pose a threat to other dogs, such as my own. I am frequently deterred from taking my dog on walks on foothill trails due to unruly dogs off leash. Additional signage is needed to inform users of single use or single direction trails. And lastly, people need to pick up their dog waste and not leave it bagged on the sides of trails!

subject: IHC Hospital on 754 South State Street
comment: The Sugar House Community Council Land Use Committee reviewed this request from the Salt Lake City Recorder's Office. We agree with the change to add 'Hospital' and 'Ambulance Services' to the allowed uses for the D-1 Central Business District Zone. This is a good location for this hospital, much easier to get to than the current LDS Hospital location. We know the University Hospital is also a Trauma hospital, and close at hand, but adding this one is a big boon to the west side of our city. Driving in a vehicle, even in a fire truck or ambulance, from the west side up to the University Hospital is difficult, especially during high traffic periods. This should allow those patients needing quick trauma care to receive that more quickly. We ask that special care be taken to locate exterior retail around that site. An entrance on the south (in addition to wherever else they put them) should allow patients and staff to use it. This will allow more foot traffic to the retail uses like Taco Time on the south. It may need a security guard, like the City Building has on the first floor, just to be sure that people entering have a reason to be there, not to just wander. We know the homeless center is nearby and don't want to make this a place where the crowds gather. They already congregate along 700 South clear up to Taufer Park. Maybe a coffee shop on the south run by IHC would help. We aren't sure exactly what the solution is, but we don't want to create another nuisance area in the city, we have enough, and at the same time, we don't want to cut off the local businesses around the building from customers. And, this is outside this request, but we learned that the old LDS Hospital will be used for physician offices. We would like you to pass along our suggestion that this might be a place where some very affordable housing could be included. This is a big building, and any place we can add affordable housing helps with our problem of not having enough housing in our city. Thank you. Judi Short, First-Vice Chair and Land Use Chair

subject: Foothills Trails Support More Trails Now
comment: Hi Council Members - Thanks for your service to the community. Please support moving forward with more trail projects in the SLC Foothills. Surveys have found data to say that 'trails' are a top priority for people in Salt Lake and State-wide. More purpose-built trails protect the environment by focusing use to thoughtfully constructed trails that require low maintenance, rather than a spiderweb of user-created trails that are erosive and may be located in undesirable areas. More trails can allow for segregated use trails to provide a better user experience for both hikers and mountain bikers. More trails improve the community and citizens' mental and physical well-being. The City Trails and Public Lands staff have done a good job of addressing the anti-trail contingent's concerns. It is well past time to restart the process of improving the Salt Lake City trail system. Please vote to restart the Foothills Trail improvement program now. Thank you-

subject: Straw Vote for the Foothill Trails
comment: I support a yes vote release the funds to construct the trails. Best, Michael

subject: Support for the Foothills Trails
comment: I'm a firm supporter of the foothills trails. Their presence in Salt Lake helps strengthen community and have been invaluable for improving the health and wellbeing of everyone who shares the trails.

subject: In support of mountain bike trails in SLC foothills
comment: Hello, I'm in support of adding and maintaining more mountain bike trails around the salt lake city valley area. It has been so nice having these in recent years. When I grew up in the Avenues in the 80s and 90s, the only trails were old jeep trails which made mountain biking difficult. It was not until the BST was added that it opened up the opportunity to explore our hills by mountain biking, and within the last ~3 years seeing more extensions (like 19th Ave, Parteys Pointe, Grandeur to Pipeline) and other trails have been wonderful. I'm a coach for the local Skyline mountain bike high school team and the Maybird club team, and having readily available trails for the kids to be able to ride from their home after school is wonderful. Above any other skill we teach our kids is courtesy and trail etiquette to make sure our kids are good stewards out on the trails. We appreciate what we have and we do not want bad behavior to spoil the opportunities available to us. Thank you so much for your work in supporting the build out of these trails so we have something nearby to enjoy. Thank you, Lars

subject: Trail Funding Vote
comment: It will be great to move forward building trails for the community. So many people love using trails. Thanks

subject: More Trails Please
comment: Please fund trails! I now drive to trails adding to congestion and pollution. My friends, who can afford to live in our city, are being attracted and choosing to live closer to established trails. I would use new foothills trails weekly to commute and exercise. My interaction with both bikers and hikers is always positive but current trails are getting crowded and dangerous. My family supports better signage - please warn innocent hikers (some with dogs) of Boosted danger or serious injury will occur. My family supports the balanced trail system previously outlined. We want a directional Dry Creek to solve that now dangerous bottleneck. We want better access to Mt. Wire and Mt. Van Cott. I believe trails draw genuine investment to our city. I really enjoyed the few new trails built but they now need some maintenance. There is so much potential in our foothills! Please fund and prioritize more trails now. Thank you for getting this needed work done!!

subject: More and better Foothill Trails Please
comment: I'm an avid mountain biker and hiker and I love to use the foothill trails close to town. There is certainly a need for more trails and improvement of existing trails. I try to avoid driving far to a trailhead so having a good mtb trail system in the foothills helps a lot. The new trails between Wild Rose and Mueller Park are fantastic. Keep it up! Regards, Robert Reich

subject: Foothills funding
comment: Hi SLC Council, I was pleased to hear you are voting on funding for the foothills trails. I am a regular with these trails and improvements are welcome. I would love to see some new trails and possibly trailhead improvements. I hope it gets approved so many locals use this system and with all the growth they can get crowded so more trails would be so nice in that area. Please approve funding Monica Torres

subject: We need a trail plan
comment: Hello, I am writing to ask that the council resume focus on and passage of the foothill trails master plan. The usage of these areas, so convenient and proximal to residential neighborhoods and downtown Salt Lake City, are seeing an increase in usage by the day. The trails plan will clarify usage, aid in minimizing environmental degradation and allow the city to maintain one of the things we love about living here: access to the outdoors. Thank you, Debra Hummet, foothill resident

subject: Please vote yes to release funds for foothill trails
comment: I ask you to release the funds on hold since 2021 for the creation of more trails in the foothill trails. Thank you!

subject: Better Foothill Trails
comment: Hello, My family enjoys the Foothill trails as much and as often as we can. We support more and better foothill trails. These trails are so important for residents. Access to trails encourage time outdoors which leads to better physical and mental health. As our population continues to grow we need to invest in opportunities for people to have access to outdoor experiences. Please support more and better Foothill trails. Kindly, Arden Clarke

subject: SLC foothills trails - Please release funding!
comment: Hello SLC Council! I'm writing to voice my approval of the release funding for the foothills trails expansion. My family of four and I regularly use the Bonneville Shoreline trail network to hike, mountain bike, walk the dog and recreate. Having such a great resource nearby means we use it nearly everyday. Additional and better trails would be awesome to have! Thanks, Chris Stepanek

subject: Foothill Trail system plan
comment: In order to truly give good feedback I'd want to go hike all of these proposed trails. Unfortunately, this is not an option because I work and have two young kids Without walking all proposed trails my feedback is... please don't build any of the biking trails like 19th Ave. 19th ave. is one of the worst built trails I have ever ridden. Thanks!

subject: SLC foothills trail support
comment: SLC Council members, I'm sending this email asking for your full support in the continued effort, maintenance and development of SLC foothill trails. As hiking, cycling and recreational has become ever more important to the community in and around. SLC, I ask for you and your council to drive support and continued efforts in keeping our kids, families and communities active in the beautiful mountains surrounding SLC. Utah is known for beautiful outdoor recreation....Let's invest in what we want our kids and communities to value and participate in. Thanks, Ben Craner

subject: Foothill trail system
comment: To whom it may concern, Me and my family are very excited that the foothill trail system will be improving and we are in strong support for funding this project! It will be nice to access these trails so close to home and decrease my driving time and adding to already congested traffic. Thanks for all you do! Adam Eresuma

subject: Foothill Trails improvements
comment: We have been property owners in Salt Lake City for twenty years now, and we love the foothill trail system. We walk and hike on these trails regularly, and we strongly support city investment in new trails/trailheads and ongoing trail maintenance. Easy access to outdoor experiences for ourselves and our kids is one of the greatest things about living in Salt Lake City. Sincerely, Amy Jameson

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: Hello, I just wanted to express my opinion regarding the funding for the planned foothill trails system. My family resides in the Salt Lake City area and we often ride mountain bikes and occasionally hike with our dogs. However, the trails near us tend to get damaged due to the crowds and we often find that many of these also lack variety in difficulty. Many others are steep and/or eroded. More trails will provide more positive experiences while also spreading the crowds. Additionally, we often travel to far trail systems and I would incredibly appreciate the availability of these trails without the long drive. I support the plan for new trails that will help meet these growing demands and provide better opportunities to appreciate nature. I'd also like to take this moment to express the idea of a fenced off walking trail in which owners are able to unleash their dogs. I'm not sure if this is the right place to pitch this but I figured it was worth a shot. Thank you so much for your time, Addison

subject: I love the trails
comment: I just wanted to write in that I love the trails that SLC has put in since 2020. I am incredibly supportive of the direction that the city is taking about would to see more progress in regards to the trails in the foothills above the Aves. Thanks for all that you are doing.

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: Hello, My name is Suzy Ricker. I love the foothill trails. I actually started using the foothill trails about 2 years ago when I started "teaching myself" to trail run. I run the trails early morning, every season and no matter what the weather is. I feel safe to run alone and the trails are an easy access from the city. I also take my dog each morning when I run and have loved having a spot where he is able to be in the mountains with me. These trails mean a lot to me and my dog and I have met several friends using the trails and there is actually a really good community of people that utilize the area. Please allow funding to help keep the trails maintained. Sincerely Suzy Ricker

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: To Whom It May Concern, I fully support more and better designed trails for all ages and users. I am a Salt Lake County resident who uses the trails weekly. We need more trails. Please release funding for more trails. Thank you! Sincerely, Michele Jakob

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: I want to express how important trails are for our community and mental health of individuals to have trails dedicated to hiking, biking and walking that are safe and allow enjoyment of this beautiful state. I consider the existence of maintained and protected trails the sign of a desirable community that is exceptional and thriving. Please promote all that is necessary to provide this great service for all to enjoy. I am very willing to fund this worthy cause through my taxes. Thank you, Phyllis Hansen

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: I was super excited to hear that the council is reprioritizing trail work in the foothills. We love these trails and can't wait to see more of them! Colin Santos

subject: Foothill trail funding!
comment: My name is Quinton Block. I have ridden mountain bikes competitively for 4 years now and I love everything about it. I work at a bike shop and have fully embraced every part of the sport, and its community. I live in sugarhouse and have utilized some paved trails like parleys to get to the foothills and friends houses. Unfortunately, I always ride right past the hills and go ride emigration instead of the hiker filled, poorly maintained, and quite frankly, boring trails along the foothills. While they do exist, trails that are fun, biker friendly, and don't have flat, blind corners are extremely hard to find. And so I either ride the road or drive my car somewhere to get to park city where the riding is good, the trails are numerous, and the turns aren't flat. I ride upwards of 15 hours a week and I'd spend 10 of those on the trails this funding would produce. With my high school team, we organize and volunteer to build and maintain trails. I know dozens of kids who would love to spend their dig days building trails that they will ride. I'm ready to not have to drive or ride my bike into PC to get to a bunch of trails. I was just getting into biking when this plan was first proposed, and I got very excited to see a new trail being built at a lookout on the way up dry creek. To my dismay, the project was abandoned and has sit vacant. I hope to see this and many other trails like it soon. Thank you for your time.

subject: I support new trails in foothill area
comment: I use the foothill trails multiple times a week with my family and friends. I love biking and hiking in the foothill area. The trails get a lot of wear and tear and are needing an upgrade. I support the project funding for new trails and trail maintenance.

subject: Foothill trail plan
comment: To whom it may concern, I am writing to show my support for expanding and going forward with the foothill trail plan. I am a SLC resident and my family and I use the foothill trails daily. More trails will lead to healthier lifestyles and ease the congestion on the small amount that are there right now. For how "outdoorsy" Utah is, SLC lags behind other major cities. I love the idea of not having to drive to use trails so I support expanding now. Thank you, Aimee Larkin

subject: Foothill trail funding
comment: I am so excited to hear the SLC council is considering foothill trails funding. I have been mountain biking on the shoreline for 25 years. I now ride with my wife and kids regularly and my kids are on the Highland High School Bike team. I strongly support moving forward to build and improve foothill trails. This can lead to a much better experience for trail users of all types (running, hiking, biking, and even winter) and a good draw for SLC as a great outdoor city. Paul Stevens

subject: Foothills trail plan
comment: I want to voice my support for more trails in and about the foothills of salt lake. I am an active user of the existing systems but with continued growth they are becoming increasingly crowded. More trails would greatly benefit the community. Best, Zach Larkin

subject: Funding for Foothill Trails
comment: My family & I moved to Salt Lake from Boulder, Colorado. We love living in Salt Lake because of the access to all the wonderful opportunities the city has to offer including the trails. We are active cyclists, runners and dog walkers. We live in the Sugarhouse area and are very excited to hear that the city council is re-prioritizing funding for the Foothills Trails. We are out on the trails around Salt Lake multiple times a week and would love to see the city move forward with improving and building more foothills trails. Thank you, Steven Hay

subject: Support for Foothill Trails Funding
comment: Dear City Council, (Darin Mano, et al) I'm excited that the SLC Council is re-prioritizing foothill trails funding. My family and I use these trails regularly for hiking, dog-walking, biking, and mountain biking, and we strongly support the city's investment in new trails, trailheads, and maintenance. The proposed trails balance environmental stewardship with quality outdoor experiences. As SLC residents, we urge you to restart funding and move forward with the approved plans. Expanding the trail network will alleviate crowding, address steep and eroded paths, and provide better access for all ages and users. We've loved the new directional and use-specific trails and look forward to seeing more improvements. Thank you for your support. Best regards, Troy Davis Salt Lake City Resident/taxpayer District 5

subject: Comments on Foothill Trails System
comment: I understand that the stalled funding for new trails may be released. I fully support this. My Dad and I use the Shoreline Trail almost daily. We enjoy it, but it's become increasingly crowded. SLC has fallen way behind other locations such as Corner Canyon as far as trail building. We could really use some additional trails to alleviate overcrowding. Thanks! Brian Morris

subject: Please get back to working on the trails!
comment: I mountain bike multiple times a week up Dry Creek and the Shoreline trails. They are crowded! Please keep building out this system with the directional trails included. Regards, Russ

subject: Foothills Trail System Plan
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Council Members, My name is Gregory Ducker and I am a Salt Lake City Avenues resident (P street and Second Avenue) and father of two young children. I'll keep this comment short and to the point. My family loves the outdoors and recreates in the Foothills all year round. My children are learning to ride their bikes in Popperton Park on the new pump track and we take family walks along the improved I street/18th Ave hiking trails. My wife and I ride the BST on mountain bikes spring through fall. We have enjoyed and taken advantage of the improvements to the foothills trails implemented in 2019-2020 and STRONGLY SUPPORT restarting trail construction to realize the vision to make the SLC foothills a welcoming place for ALL trail users of all ages. When we moved here in 2018, there was no way-finding and severely eroded hiking trails with many conflicts between users. We were so excited when construction started on the implementation of the new foothills plans that prioritized accessibility and openness to all. The SLC foothills are a gift to all residents of the city and the valley and improving access leads to more outdoor recreation opportunities and reduces emissions from driving to more distant trailheads that currently feature more family-friendly trails and services. We are so excited to raise our family in Salt Lake City and hope that a more welcoming and accessible foothills trail system can soon be completed for our children to use. subject: Foothill Trail Work
comment: Hello- My family and I use the Foothill trail system multiple times per week for hiking, trail running and biking. We are greatly in favor of SLC resuming the paused trail construction. - we far prefer using trails close by, without a long drive to Millcreek or other areas. - we are greatly in favor of biking only/ foot traffic only trails as single user trails are far, far safer for all user groups. - the user traffic on trails has greatly, greatly increased on SLC Foothill trails. As the population of SLC continues to grow so rapidly, so too does the proportion of the local population that uses the trail network. SLC has the unique opportunity to make SLC a truly world - class, outdoor- focused city by improving the trail network. - the Foothills are already criss-crossed by miles of dis-used and underutilized trails that need to be improved and maintained. These old trails are relics of past utility work and not designed to accommodate foot or bike traffic. If these trails were to be improved for modern use the foothills would be a safer and more enjoyable experience for all users. Thank you, Matt

subject: Support for Foothill Trails System
comment: Our family uses the Salt Lake City trail system multiple times a week for hiking, walking our dog and biking. We support City investment in new trails, trailheads, and ongoing trail maintenance. We strongly believe having updated trail systems will improve our family's and all of Salt Lake City resident's quality of life with increased access to our mountains, promoting environmental stewardship. - James Alfandre Bonneville Hills Community Council Chair

subject: Foothills trails
comment: Hello, my name is Max Miles and I want to voice my opinion that these trials should be made and renewed and that our cities lacking new trails and updating trails by other cities. Come on step up your game.

subject: Foothills trails
comment: Thank you for providing funding for improving our well-loved and heavily used Foothills Trails. We hike on them several times a week. We often have conversations with others about how wonderful it is to have these trails so close to our homes, so that all of us can get out and hike, even if we don't have time to drive to the mountains. We LOVE our Foothills Trails. Please keep improving and adding new sections, so hikers of all abilities can enjoy this health-giving, mentally-uplifting, activity! C Clark and R Gamble 84103

subject: Foothills trails
comment: Dear Council Members and Mayor Mendenhall, My family uses the Foothill trails for hiking, jogging and mountain biking every week. A masterplan was approved, started, paused and adjusted, each of them necessary steps to learn and adjust. About 8 years have passed and now, the current trails are crowded and in need of repair. The large number of users creates safety hazards, and results in user conflicts. Many side trails have been created, causing more erosion (and substandard trails). It is time for action. We need trails! My family supports investment in new trails, trail maintenance, signage, user education, and whatever it takes to get more trails in place. Let's create improved outdoor recreation opportunities for our residents and visitors. To me, this is a much higher priority than building a new sports district downtown. Best Regards, Nancy Schmaus

subject: SLC trails
comment: Just wanted to say how excited I am about the prospect of expanding our trails for hiking and mountain biking in SLC foothills. Good trail networks are such a great investment in the community. Areas like Park City, Draper and Herriman have done such an amazing job- hopefully Salt Lake can do something similar

subject: Foothill trail improvements please!
comment: Hi, we're a family of 6 who use the foothill trails at least 3 days a week. We bike, trail run and hike. We're also high school mountain bike coaches with two mountain biking daughters on a local team. Riding bikes FROM our house is what makes SLC truly special. What other great city also has recreational trails in their backyard? Riding bikes with peers has been life changing for our girls. It promotes grit, outdoor stewardship, healthy and strong bodies and an awesome co-ed community. Junior High and High school mountain biking is exploding in the Salt Lake Valley but trails are getting crowded. We love the new biking only and directional trails. They're great for people doing a range of activities (hikers don't have to deal with bikers, etc), promote safety and help unclog the trails. SLC has already outgrown our small trail system and we often have to go to Park City or Bountiful or Draper. Let us skip the drive and stay in town! SLC growth isn't pausing so please unpause the foothill trail funding. Please, please, please and thank you! Sincerely, Nicole Fisher

subject: In support of trail funding
comment: Hello, Council! I am a frequent trail user (dog walking, hiking, mountain biking) and I urge you to prioritize funds for trail building. More and more people are out and about as evidenced by the huge uptick in use I've seen in the last 30 years. I see college kids behind the U running, older folks like me loop through with our dogs, and how great is it that high schoolers want to get out and race mountain bikes! I wish I'd had that opportunity when I was younger. You have my full support to fund more trails in Salt Lake City. Sincerely, Kate Ferguson

subject: KSL article on what Utahns thing of raising taxes
comment: As a resident living in Downtown Salt Lake, I am very upset by Victoria Petro's comment calling me and my fellow Utahns "average constituents." With a statement like that, I'm wondering what all members of the City Council really feel about us. A public apology is certainly in order here. Douglas and Nancy Kohler.

subject: Encouragement to expand foothill trail
comment: I just wanted to emphasize the importance of the trail system to our family and community. Specifically to the youth in the area. So many of our youth are spending time outside exercising on our mountain bike trails. My 14 year old daughter who said she wasn't really sure she wanted to join in mountain biking said "high school is really stressful. But as soon as I ride on the trails in the afternoon, all my stress goes away and I feel like I can do my homework and everything else the rest of the evening. It's like it just makes everything feel manageable." I can't think of a better way for our teenagers to be using their time. Working on their physical and mental health in the area that we are lucky to live so close by. Please allow funds for the expansion of this trail system. Allison (Hallie) Keller

subject: SLC Foothills Trails Funding
comment: Dear SLC Council- I was recently made aware that you will be voting tomorrow whether to, or not to, release funding for Foothill Trails System improvements. I hope you vote to release the funds for these proposed improvements. Outdoor recreation is a major factor in many local SLC residents' lives, as well as an attraction for people visiting SLC and Utah in general. The addition of purpose-built (some for hiking, some for biking) and directional trails above the Avenues a few years ago were a great addition. But given the growing population of the city, more trails would not go unappreciated. Especially the building of directional and/or user specific trails in order to improve trail safety and to enhance individual user experience. Thank you for your consideration on this topic that is important to myself and so many other SLC residents. Sincerely, Mike Bisignani SLC Utah

subject: Foothills Trail development
comment: My name is Jamie Kent. I grew up on 18th Ave in SLC. The foothills across the street from my house were my stomping grounds. In the foothills, I learned how to ride my bike on dirt, hike, play , hunt, collect critters and ski. What a wonderful place to grow up! Back in the day, it was only me and my friends that frequented the area. We would spend entire days exploring only to return home when the sun went down without seeing another soul. I look back on those days with nostalgia, I was one of the lucky ones to have such an experience. Since the 2002 Winter Olympics came to SLC, we have seen crazy growth throughout the valley and especially for outdoor recreation. There is not much we can do about this growth but embrace it. One important way to embrace the growth is to plan, and create more trails so the crowds can disperse. By developing more multi-use trails in the foothills, we are making this a better place for all. We need more trails! The crowds are not going away, they will continue to seek the foothills no matter what, more trails will help protect certain areas of the foothills from degradation. It would be extremely short sighted if we were to halt the trail development plan. Please move forward with implementing the plan. Jamie Kent

subject: Fund the Trails
comment: SAC Council: We desperately need to finish the trail system around Salt Lake. It is crowded up there, and it is not safe (or, at least, it could be a lot safer). I recognize that there are strong feelings on both sides of these issues, but the reality is that there are already a lot of people using the trails and the number will only increase. The environmental impact of trail traffic is inevitable, and so simply needs to be managed. Further, more and better trails will decrease the off-trail use, necessitate by "shortcuts" by bikers and hikers to avoid each other. Further, the trails are very close to SLC, an urban environment. It is not unreasonable to put people into the Foothills. There is lots of untouched, or hardly-touched space as one get higher/further away from the City. Among other things, separating bikes and hikers is a good idea. We all find ways to get along, and are happy to share the trails, but at the same time it is a relief when we have our own paths. And, again, it is a safety issue. So, please, please fund finishing the existing trails and adding more. James E. Magleby MAGLEBY CATAXINOS, PC

subject: Please release funding for SLC Trails
comment: Hello, I am writing to encourage the council to immediately release all funds for trail building and maintenance in Salt Lake City. I am a hiker and mountain biker who utilizes the foothill trails 4x a week. Here are some of my experiences that indicate why the investment is so overdue: • I walk my dog in the foothills 2-3x a week. He is always leashed and curbed when we hike, and he has a leash aggression. This means when non-leashed dogs approach him (despite me telling the dog owners to recall their dog as mine is not friendly) he often attacks them. This occurs 2-3x per walk. Per walk. Please, use these funds to make it clear what areas/trailheads are on-leash and off-leash areas, and then enforce infractions. • The quantity of dog waste left behind, whether in a poop bag or not, is staggering. I worry if the waste problems continue to increase, all dogs will be uninvited from the shoreline trails. While this would be sad, I would understand the reasoning. Please help provide more waste receptacle, more education, and consequences for those who do not pick up after their dog. • While biking, I have been attacked twice by off leash dogs. One of them caught me and broke the skin on my ankle. Countless times while biking I have had to stop or risk hitting unleashed dogs blocking the trail. • Also while biking, I have been accosted several times by hikers and trail runners. They are complaining about my group size, or when we arrive at blind corners at the same time. I understand the frustration, but do not condone the tone or language they choose to use with me. In Park City, I've noticed an improvement in hiker/biker relations after they launched their "10 seconds to be kind" campaign with trailhead signage. • If you use our trails, you know the number of people on them is significantly higher every year. Please cut more trails. Make the unidirectional, single use, and equitable. We are surrounded by other cities and counties who have figured out how to cut trails all trail users can enjoy. Please, let Salt Lake City learn from them and become a leader in how to properly manage mountain access so that all may safely enjoy them. Thanks, Marcus Cazier

subject: Foothills Trail System
comment: Hello, I am reaching out to express my thoughts on the Foothill Trail System. I believe that there is a huge need to add and create more outdoor trails in the Salt Lake City area. The trail system we have is overloaded. I am an avid cyclist and mountain biker, and I have lived beneath the Foothills my whole life, and love spending time in the Wasatch mountains with my family. I am also a coach of the local Highschool mountain bike team. We desperately need expansion to make way for a new generation of outdoor enthusiasts born here and for all those who continue to move here to take advantage of. I believe that the opportunity to get outside increases health, happiness and forms a stronger sense of community. I believe that we are behind on creating more outdoor space here salt lake compared to other neighboring cities. Let's build our own "Corner Canyon" where we can have multi use trails that won't be over crowded. Where our Highschools can practice close to home, and our community will have more options and opportunities to connect with each other and with the beauty of the city we live in. Thanks Kristin Anderson

subject: Support for funding Foothill Trail System
comment: Hello, As a long time resident of Salt Lake I want to express my support of funding the new trail improvements for the Foothill Trail system. Over the years Salt Lake's population has grown and we need to increase the number of trails and improve them. This will allow all trail users to use the trails in a safe manner, creating one way, or single-use trails as needed. Please help Salt Lake stay awesome and give us easy access to world class views and recreation. Thanks Dyan

subject: Foothills trails funding
comment: Hi, I am a 23 year resident of Salt Lake City and use the trails from Parley's to City Creek regularly. I am a multi use user, bike hike and dog walk! I fully support more funding and continuing expansion of the trail system. With the continuing growth and increased use I think the approach of including directional and some use specific trails will be helpful too. The sooner the better! Thanks for continuing to work and care for our foothills. Hugh Ferguson HSF Construction Inc.

subject: Trails
comment: Please vote no on the release of funds to widen the living room and other trails. A Very bad idea and I love hiking on the foothills!

subject: Foothills Trails
comment: Please Provide More and Better SLC foothill now. We really need them, I love the new Trail! The heels not wheel and the wheel not heel directional specific trails which is awesome. We need more of those please, Thank you! Bye bye

subject: Foothills Trail System Master Plan
comment: Dear Council, I'm writing in favor of proceeding with the Foothills Trail System Master Plan. This project, which was well-crafted and designed in the first place, has been on hold long enough. I grew up using the shoreline trail, hiking Mount Wire, and riding my bike on Bobsled in the late 90s and early 2000s. It's hard for me to believe that we still have essentially the same trail system in place when so many of the other cities along the Wasatch Front have invested heavily in their trails and made something really special for hikers, runners, and mountain bikers. We can do this with our trail system. We can do it in a sustainable way. And we can make it great for our kids and for their kids. The Master Plan, while not perfect, is a good starting point, and it is time to push aside the few loud voices that have kept the project from moving forward. From my perspective, the few trails that were constructed in 2020--particularly the new uphill trail from Memory Grove and the 19th Ave. downhill trail--were well-routed, nicely built, and clearly marked. Although they looked rough when first built, it should be obvious to all that the cuts into the mountainside were temporary and the vegetation quickly grew back as hoped. In short, let's get this moving, and let's catch up with the rest of the Wasatch Front. -- Spencer Brown

subject: Trails
comment: I am writing to encourage the Council to remove the existing hold on the trail construction funding. I use the Foothill Trail system multiple times a week biking, hiking and trail-running by myself and with my family. We love the new trails at Parley's Point improving and expanding the trail system is important for staying active.

subject: Foothills Trails
comment: Hi my name is Greg Foster and I'm the SLC resident of the avenue and I'm calling in for the advocate for the expansion of the Foothill Trails . I've been on the trails all the time and bringing my dog. I'd like to ask the SLC Council to vote yes on this. Thank you so much. Bye

subject: Foothills Trails
comment: Hi, My name is Annabelle Olsen. I wanted to call to keep the Trails open, I know that me and my friends love going there a lot, we love it there. Please keep the trail open. Thank you!

subject: Funding for Foothill trails
comment: I urge you to reinstate funding for the construction and development of sustainable, accessible trails in the foothills. Our mountains and foothills are amazing assets that should be used—but in a carefully planned out way; this funding makes that possible. Adding well-thought out trails will add value to our community and has the potential to improve the quality of life of everyone who chooses to use the trails. Please invest in the unique and amazing geography we have here in Salt Lake!

subject: Foothills Trail Plan
comment: Hello, I'm calling to support the foothill Trails Funding to build trails in the foothill. My name is Philip Blevins and I hard support on the doing the work on the foothill trails. I'm highly support the funds to use toward the trail that we have

subject: Support for more mountain biking trails in Salt Lake City
comment: Salt Lake City Council, I understand you'll be reviewing the Foothills Master Plan soon. I love mountain biking, hiking, backpacking, and other recreational activities. Salt Lake City has unparalleled access to mountain recreation, but as our population has grown and the popularity of outdoor activities has increased, Salt Lake City needs to do more. Salt Lake City has lagged behind Draper, Lehi, Herriman and Spanish Fork in developing new trails and promoting outdoor recreation. The other Cities have benefited substantially by investing in new trails and promoting healthy outdoor activities. The trails around SLC are at capacity, and user conflicts are increasing. The City needs many more Mountain Bike specific trails. Mountain biking has experienced exponential growth over the last 3 years and we need more trails to properly enjoy our foothills. I am writing to voice my support for the Foothills Master Plan. The newly completed trails in the Foothills are fantastic, and I'd love to see phase 1 completed and phase 2 begun on schedule. Please don't heed to the loud minority who hate mountain bikers and want to stop the creation of more trails. I appreciate your consideration. Sincerely, Heather

subject: Expand the Foothill trail system
comment: I am a high school senior and an avid mountain biker and hiker. I love our foothill trail system and I am an advocate for expanding our trails. I think that the main reason that we have these foothill trails is to get people out of the city/valley and into the mountains. We need new trails in order to get new people into the mountains without having to drive 30-40 minutes into park city or up the canyons. I know that expanding the trail system will give Utah people: hiking, biking, or just walking a better chance to get outdoors and enjoy the mountains of Utah

subject: Foothills trail system plan
comment: Hello, This is Matt Peters, SLC resident and I'm calling in interested to comment about the foothill trails system and excited to get going again. I'm happy for the trail but I'm concerning about the Erosion issues so as they didn't mess up the erosion because it's just a pain. Thank you!

subject: Foothills trail system plan
comment: Hello, I'm calling to encourage the council to release the funding for the plan for the foothill trail since 2021 and I know that there's some vote's going on tomorrow for release the funds. Thank you!

subject: Fund our trails
comment: Hi, I am a mother to an avid mtn biker and also a resident in neighboring Harvard/yale area. I am emailing to express my support of funding and expanding our local foothill trails. It is so important to us to have our Slc trail system expanded and fully funded to provide safe, close, and use of public land for our families. Residents of the foothills do not own the mountains or their trails. We are so lucky to live in this beautiful valley full of trails and mountains to enjoy. Let's keep it that way! Best, Chelsea Horsley

subject: Foothill Trails System Improvements
comment: I would like to voice my support of releasing the city funding for improving and adding to our foothill trail system. Our current trails are over crowded and in need up repairs. We need more trails to be accessible closer to home. My family uses the Salt Lake City trails several times a week for hiking, biking, and cross country skiing in the winter. We see the need for new trails to meet the growing demand and ensure positive experiences for all trail users. Thank you!

subject: Continue funding bike, hiking and walking paths in Salt Lake City
comment: Please continue funding the trail system in the Salt Lake City area. These are important to the residents that live here. It is nice to have a place to go ride, walk and hike.

subject: Trail System Improvements
comment: I'm reaching out to support the release of city funds to improve and expand our foothill trail system. My family uses the Salt Lake City trails multiple times a week for hiking, biking, and cross-country skiing, and we've noticed how overcrowded and in need of repairs the trails have become. We believe it's important to make more trails accessible closer to home to meet the growing demand. Expanding and enhancing the trail system will ensure a positive experience for all users. Thank you for considering this initiative! Ken Montague

subject: Please Fully Fund and Expand the Foothills Trail System Plan
comment: City Council: I am a Salt Lake City resident and father of four boys, and we are avid hikers and cyclists. I am a competitive trail runner and cyclist, a mountain bike coach, and an advocate for Utah's open spaces. In the fall of 2015, when I was a member of Salt Lake City's Parks, Natural Lands, Urban Forestry, and Trails Board, I approached Lewis Kogan with some concerns regarding trails in the Foothills. I have witnessed many, and even been involved in, user conflicts while recreating on those trails. I have been bitten by an off-leash pitbull, detained my sons when chased by off-leash dogs, been hit by a descending mountain biker in Dry Creek, and been yelled at by hikers claiming that the Foothills are off limits to bikes. Lewis and I discussed some of those issues. I asked that the City consider adopting a plan and formally adopting and expanding the trails system, and I have followed the proceedings rather closely since then. I have recreated in SLC's Foothills for as long as I can remember (even back when we could drive trucks from North Salt Lake to the radio towers above Ensign Peak). They are one of the things I missed most while living out of state for eight years. Although I returned 15 years ago, I'm daily in awe of the Foothills and the peaks they sometimes hide. They've built in my sons and me an appreciation for nature, a love for our natural resources, and a desire to protect our open spaces. My spouse was hit by a drunk driver while riding her bike eight years ago; while I previously spent thousands of miles on a road bike each year, that episode changed us. We sought refuge in the Foothills—running, hiking, and biking to escape, if only for a moment, our own thoughts and the noise of city life. I recently created a map of my activities in the Foothills, and that map shows hits blanketed in red lines where I've seen elk, moose, mountain lion, and countless fellow runners, hikers, and bikers. My sons joined NICA (the high school mountain bike league, of which Utah's over 7,000 student-athletes make it the country's largest chapter), and the Foothills have become their escape—whether from a long day at school, peer pressure, and especially during the days of social distancing, remote learning, and Zoom classes. As a dad and coach on our East High team, I've loved introducing new riders to the Foothills, whether overlooking This is the Place State Park at sunset, marveling at spring's balsam root-covered hills, or peering into City Creek Canyon (forbidden to mountain bikes). Our team has more than doubled in size in the last three years, and other teams at City schools (including West, Highland, Judge, SLCSE, and a Composite team from other area schools) have seen similar growth. We're teaching these hundreds of new trail users to exercise appropriate etiquette, to care for their public lands, to give back by helping maintain trails, and to encourage their families and friends to do the same. In fact, the response from these kids has on more than one occasion overwhelmed the City's capacity to accommodate the kids' volunteer requests—even when they're working on hiking-only trails! Anticipating increasing demands for trail space, and being disappointed at seeing Salt Lake City fall behind cities throughout the West in trail building (whether conservative cities like Bountiful, Draper, Herriman, St. George, and Boise, or progressive cities like Moab, Boulder, and Park City) were some of the motivations behind my discussions with Lewis back in 2015 about a plan that would permit City residents to recreate from their homes, rather than having to drive to Draper or the Wasatch Back (it's silly to have to drive a car to ride a bike). Years later, I was happy to hear that the City adopted a plan (following public input) to give its residents better access to its Foothills with more, better trails. The BST (and its large number of social-trail offshoots, many of which are unsustainable, and some of which suffer severe erosion) is great but overcrowded, rife with user conflict, and insufficient for a city like SLC. I have been thrilled to see the City build new trails and excited to see the new plan be implemented. There are (and should be expected) growing pains and where favorites are closed and new cuts look raw, but we need more sustainable trails to replace some of the social and unsustainable trails of the past. Reworking some of the new trails, and giving all of the new trails time to become established, has been a positive thing for the growing network. But it's not enough. Where appropriate, users could be separated to provide a better, safer experience. And while I'll miss running some of the trails I used to run, or riding some of the trails I used to ride, I am thrilled to see a generation of runners and riders learn to love our open spaces, discover there is more to life than Minecraft, and accomplish challenges they previously found daunting. The City went to great lengths to inventory public lands, get public input, develop a plan, get input on that plan, and adopt that plan. Now, despite how many people love the new trails, a few disgruntled neighbors have halted progress. They have been supported in this effort by Save Our Canyons, of which I was a supporter for many years, because influential donors have cornered Save Our Canyons into an effort in which SOC wouldn't otherwise involve themselves (and have no history of so doing). When I discussed with the then-executive director of SOC the need for more trails in a city our size, his response was: 'couldn't your middle and high school kids do their mountain bike training on city roads instead? This 'recreate in my way or don't recreate at all' mentality has won the day and halted much-needed trail building. I run and ride on the City's trails as much as anyone, and I simply don't understand the mindset. I contend that much of the effort from Save Our Foothills is not as much about trails or balsam root as it is about control. Their neighborhoods have been more impacted than most by rude and loud users (runners and riders alike—I've even seen motorcycles at Morris Meadows); by people illegally parking in areas where parking is already pinched; etc. Clearly, something needs to be done. But SOF were conspicuously quiet when the University of Utah tore up the Foothills in connection with the water tower construction. They were again quiet when the bulldozers and tankers turned the area behind the medical center into a construction site, burying old trails and displacing countless users, creating massive dirt roads that have yet to be fixed. No SOF protests, no signs—I'm guessing because it didn't impact their parking despite the massive and permanent hillside scarring (including a new paved road) and crushed balsam root. The fact is that more trails are better for everyone, and a variety of trails is better for everyone. While I enjoy riding a bike downhill, I don't believe that every trail should be a downhill mountain bike trail. As a hiker and runner, I don't believe that all trails should be accessible only to those on foot. That said, it makes sense to separate uses at times. Take the Armstrong trail in Park City, for example: it is one of the most beloved of the 500+ miles of trails in Park City because it lets hikers and runners peacefully co-exist with uphill-only riders, who must find another place to descend. There are many ways to travel above, below, and through the Mid-Mountain area, but Mojave is limited to downhill bikes only, which means I can run in that area and generally not have to worry about conflicts with riders. The City should fully fund, build, maintain, and expand the approved plan, because: • Cities throughout Utah and the Intermountain West are building trails at a rapid pace to keep up with increasing use, population growth, and increasing user conflict (user conflict can come from traffic not appropriately yielding, congestion, improper trail use [e.g., off-leash dogs in leash-restricted areas in SLC], etc. • Salt Lake City lags behind local municipalities like Draper, Herriman, and cities in Davis County (not to mention Park City, Moab, and St. George), in sustainable trail miles, while having a larger population than all of them combined. Salt Lake City lags far behind regional cities like Boise, Denver, Boulder, and Phoenix in trail building as well. • Many of Salt Lake City's trails are social trails – trails created by foot and/or animal traffic, which are unsustainable, prone to erosion, and provide a poor user experience. These trails are not environmentally friendly and are not user friendly. Even the most dismissive viewer would acknowledge that the rutted fat-tire trail near the JCC is in terrible condition and dangerous—it has sent my son to the hospital on a crash from his bike, and it has left me bruised and bloodied from a fall while running. • Cities find significant economic benefit when building trails – as users have a better experience, they visit a city more often and spend more money locally. • Given the dearth of suitable trails in SLC, accommodating the approximately 300 kids enrolled in mountain bike programs at Salt Lake City public schools requires those teams often drive those 300 kids (plus coaches and parents) to Park City, Draper, or other local trails, multiple times per week—this is not great for our vehicle traffic and air pollution concerns. This is true of other riders as well—many riders find themselves having to drive to distant trailheads because of overcrowding and lack of suitable trails in Salt Lake City. • Utah High School Mountain Bike League growth is up exponentially, with the league splitting into two regions in 2016, three regions in 2018, four regions in 2020, and six regions in 2022 with over 7,000 student athletes. • Student athletes from Millcreek, Holladay, Draper, Woods Cross, North Salt Lake, and bountiful often ride in Salt Lake City given the low-elevation trails with soils conducive to early season riding. • Bike sales surged 69% in 2020 vs 2019, and have only grown since then. • The demands placed on Salt Lake City's trails (few of which are suitable for beginners or lower intermediate riders) are skyrocketing. The need for trails has never been greater, and the demands are only likely to increase as the thousands of new youth riders in Utah are bringing young friends and older family members into the sport. • Trail running and hiking are also seeing increasing popularity. Increasing user conflict is best ameliorated by adding trail miles and by separating user types where appropriate (such as multi-use uphill traffic and downhill foot traffic on one trail with downhill bike traffic on a nearby trail—this works everywhere and is common in Draper, Park City, Telluride, Boulder, Sun Valley, Boise, and other places with planned trail systems). • The City has five goals for the new trails system: o Environmentally Sustainable: Trails avoid sensitive habitat, minimize erosion, and make efficient use of available natural lands while protecting the wild and scenic nature of the Foothills landscape. o Enjoyable: Trails cater to a diversity of recreation types and users, and a variety of desired experiences. o Accessible: Trails are accessible to a broad audience of beginner to intermediate trail users, including families, seniors, and people with disabilities. o Safe: Trail user conflicts are mitigated and minimized through trail design and use regulations. o Low-Maintenance: Trails drain water naturally, follow contours instead of fat-lines, and encourage users to remain on-trail, minimizing maintenance efforts. All of the City's goals for the new trails system (environmentally sustainable, enjoyable, accessible, safe, and low-maintenance) can be achieved under the current plan. The City should build out (and even expand) the current plan as rapidly as possible, and the City should remain committed to being responsive when problems arise (such as the City's quick response to the sloughing and poor design that plagued the first few hundred feet of the new East City Creek trail, which is now a much better and safer experience). Progress upsets people, but please: let's not let a few disgruntled folks keep the City from achieving its potential and staying true to its identity as a mecca for outdoor recreation. Instead, let's work to resolve issues as they arise and support the City in creating a world class trails system offering a great experience for all users. Please fully fund, implement, and expand the Foothill Trails System Plan. I am happy to discuss further at your convenience. Thank you,

subject: We need more trails!
comment: As a father of 5 kids in the Salt Lake District, I am pleading with you to help find ways for our kids to get outside. We regularly use these trails but they are very crowded at times. We need more trails to accommodate all different levels of riders for our kids and families.

Life is tough. We need more trails in our foothills. Please. Fwiw, I live on Virginia st and see the parking for MTB grow up the street every year. People need places to ride! Let's go! Parker McBrief

subject: Unfortunate Save Our Foothills Lies
comment: Council Members- Although I normally would not take time to make negative remarks, this time I am compelled. Trails Utah has been working with the University and USFS to plan much needed trail maintenance on the Living Room area trails. That included funding from a local donor in Research Park and a UDOR grant. This is a project to complete basic trail maintenance. Last week we took time to field review the project with Councilperson Dugan, Trails and Public Lands staff, the University, USFS, and Save Our Foothills. Save Our Foothills representatives made outrageous untrue claims such as 'widening a trail 6' during maintenance will disrupt animals crossing the trail' and that 'dirt from trail maintenance will be visible from the SLC Airport'. Previously they claimed that the new Parleys Pointe BST was causing the whole hillside to collapse, which is not true. Then today they sent out a flier saying that planning trail maintenance subverted the new trail construction moratorium, which it does not. Simply put, Save Our Foothills is a group of NIMBYs that makes outrageous claims and lies to meet their intent to have no new trails, no improvements to trails, and no maintenance on trails. They do not represent the majority opinion nor do they have the public interest in mind. John Knoblock

subject: Foothills Living Room trail
comment: As I'm sure you're aware, Save Our Foothills has warned of a threat to the popular Living Room Trail in the foothills behind the University of Utah. It seems that the same private trail builder that did environmental damage in other parts of the Foothills has secured secretive funding to widen the Living Room trail to 3 feet. Foothills trails should be a popular project with broad public support, but mismanagement has made the public mistrustful. This trail is a favorite of people in Salt Lake City. Let's not ruin it. Trail construction should be halted until it can be done with full transparency and public support for the plan.

subject: More trails please!
comment: I am writing to ask you to please re-instate the Foothill trail expansion project. I use the trails multiple times a week with my family, the jr. high and high school mountain bike team, and my friends. The trails we have are amazing and so much fun. But we need more. We have so few trails, that I very often have to travel to Park City or Bountiful to have access to more trails. It doesn't have to be that way. We have the land, we just need the trails. Thank you for the addition of the 19th Ave trail a few years ago. It is so much fun and has added variety and much needed mileage in trails close to home. The trails we have are such an asset to Salt Lake but there just aren't enough. Please keep adding trails. The mountains are at our doorsteps, let the community enjoy them. We need more trails to help meet the needs of our growing population. We need more trails so we can teach our kids and future generations respect and love for the natural resources in our own backyard. We have the space to do it, so please let us use it. Many thanks, Alison Crockett & kids

subject: foothill trails

subject: It's past time
comment: It's past time we restarted building. The plan has been in place, talked about, reworked to the point that the next issue will be that it's too old! It's time to start moving dirt.

subject: STRONG SUPPORT for new and improved and expanded Foothill Trails
comment: Hello and thank you for your time. I am a Salt Lake City resident, and want to express my support and request for expanded and improved SLC Foothill trails. We have a huge opportunity to have an amazing trail system in our Foothills, for our entire community to use and enjoy. This is a very under-tapped gem and resource that has so much potential! With specific and intentional trails (designed mountain biking, hiking/trail running, and multi-use trails we can all use and enjoy our public lands together, while cutting down on misuse, "cow paths" and confusion. While I understand that Foothill residents have their gripes and concerns, the Foothills are all of our public land to use. I hope that with intentional planning, and respect, the citizens who have a right to enjoy these lands can do so with respect and gratitude for accessing and parking in these neighborhoods. Salt Lake City residents should not have to travel to Draper, Park City, Bountiful, and many other communities who are doing a much better job with trails than we are. I use the trails regularly as an avid mountain biker, hiker and trail runner. My wife and daughter use them daily as well. It is a community, and part of OUR community. I am a volunteer coach for the East High School Mountain Bike team (Utah High School Cycling League/ National Interscholastic Cycling Association) We use the trails regularly, but more often must travel with multiple vehicles and students to other destinations where the trail networks are far superior. It is time for Salt Lake City to create and maintain an expansive, comprehensive Foothill trail system for ALL community members to enjoy! Thank you for your time. Jake Ricker Salt Lake City, UT

comment: I am writing to express my strong support for the Department of Public Lands decision to continue with the Foothills Trail Project. I am a resident of the upper avenues, and live nearby several key trailheads and parking areas. I use the trails almost daily for walking, hiking, running, and biking. They are a tremendous and underused resource. I hope the Department of Public Lands will continue to expand the number of trails, to improve existing trails, and make other investments at trailheads to accommodate current and future users. I look forward to your trail crews resuming work soon. Many thanks! Adam Looney (and family)
