Rather than having them commute to Park City or Davis County in order to practice and exercise I'd like for them have that opportunity here, locally. We have a lot of people in Salt Lake that want to hike, ride or run close to home. Please support the Foothill Trail System. Thanks, Peter Harrison

subject: Foothills Master Plan
comment: Hey Darin, I just wanted to reach out and offer my support for building more trails in our foothills. I run, hike, or mountain bike in the foothills multiple times per week and often access these trails from my doorstep (in your district, a few short miles of biking/transit away). Spending time before and after work in these close-by natural areas is one of my favorite things about living in SLC. It's ridiculous that this plan has been delayed for 4+ years after 5+ years of planning and stakeholder input. We need more trails for both hiking/running and mountain biking and we need trailhead infrastructure to support a growing number of users. A small, but vocal and wealthy minority cannot continue to keep that from happening. Communities to the south (Draper), north (Bountiful/Farmington), east (PC), and west (Herriman/Daybreak) have all been building more trails and increasing recreation opportunities for their residents while Salt Lake City has remained in gridlock over this plan. The foothills of SLC are incredibly special, but an unofficial network of social trails that has gone largely unmaintained and unimproved for decades no longer supports the needs of this community. We can figure out some of the details along the way (I would love to see less legacy trail closures and more trail additions), but a hard pause on this construction lasting any longer is a total failure of our local government. Please support the Foothills Master Plan moving forward. I'm really looking forward to running and biking on new trails in the near future. Thanks, Austin Whitehead

subject: Foothill Trails Master Plan
comment: Dear City Council Members, While I have spent many years participating in public feedback sessions on this topic, I'm submitting yet another feedback comment regarding the Foothills Master Plan. During your vote on 8/27, and as a homeowner near the Terrace Hills trails access point, I request that you reinstate the paused Foothills Trails Plan. There is no reason to stop the implementation of the original plan. No Native American objection. No geological erosion reason. No harm to wildlife. Our city and our community need more trails created for use-specific recreation as our population continues to grow. While re-implementing the plan is priority number 1, I would implore you to consider the original Foothills plan as it was drafted: with trails like the "sword of Zworo" above Morris Meadow restored to use as "hike and uphill bike access only" and the foothills ridge trails returned to public use without the use of trenches and fences. Thanks for your consideration, Josh Rhea

subject: Funding needed for Trails!
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Council, I am writing to you today to respectfully request that you release funds that were originally set aside three years ago for the care and management of the Foothills Natural Area through the implementation of the SLC Foothill Trails Master Plan. This plan took almost three years to develop, involved dozens of open houses and public input opportunities, and is desperately needed to help manage ongoing impacts from recreational activity affecting one of Salt Lake City's greatest assets; the open space of the foothills. Withholding funds will result in further degradation to the landscape, erode the trail user experience, and firmly establish the Salt Lake City foothills as one of the most poorly managed and maintained open space areas next to any major urban center in the west. The popularity of outdoor recreation in all it's forms, hiking, running, dog walking, mountain biking, is only going to increase and we must engage these trends and work to do what is best for the foothills and our outdoor-loving population. Trails Utah is dedicated to helping connect people to Utah's spectacular landscapes through sustainably built trails while helping preserve the integrity of our natural open spaces and the eco-systems they support. We are here to facilitate this process and partner with the City, the University, and others who share these values. Unfortunately, there are those who paint our efforts as deceitful, destructive, and antithetical to the values of creating a sustainable human presence in the foothills and are opposing the release of these needed resources. This is deeply disheartening as we all care about the natural beauty and environmental integrity of our shared foothills. Trails Utah initiated a stakeholder development and visioning effort to better manage and improve foothill trails in 2015, shortly after we became established as a non-profit. Our initial effort was supported by the Eccles Foundation before Salt Lake City stepped forward to invest in the trails master planning process. Trails Utah is incredibly grateful for the City's efforts and applauds Salt Lake City Trails and Public Lands for the outstanding job they have done to address concerns about communicating about the plan, the engagement process, conducting studies and adressing environmental concerns, and ensuring trails are properly designed and constructed. They are thoroughly deserving of your support and should be allowed to go forward and do the good work they are capable of. I appreciate your time and consideration of this matter. Sincerely, Sarah Bennett

subject: Foothill Trails Funding
comment: Dear City Council, I'm Max, I'm a 15-year-old mountain biker and I live in the Avenues. I ride the trails near my house like the BST, 19th Ave, and Bobsled all the time. I also ride with my high school mountain bike team and we train in the foothills during the spring and fall when it's cooler. I was pretty excited when I saw the original Foothills Master Plan that detailed many trails that were supposed to be built. I followed the trail building at Popperton and up higher closely. It was pretty disappointing when the build was paused after just a year. The current trails we have in the Avenues are good but there just aren't enough. This leads to a high concentration of people on one trail. This can be a big issue when our training groups for mountain bike team encounter a ton of other trail users as compared to other systems in the area. We could also use a larger variety of mountain bike trail types to promote progression and build skills. When trails like these are built, the local teams would be happy to put in work on them in a condition that suits both riders and wildlife in the foothills. Thanks, Max Peterson

subject: Artesian well park at 6th S. & 5th E.
comment: I went to the park one morning last week and there were probably 20 unhoused individuals using it as a campground. I certainly sympathize with the plight of the homeless, but surely there are better areas where they can camp than at a park where people come at all hours to fill their water jugs and expect some modicum of sanitation. While I was there, one woman even had her dog jump up on the water filling station for a drink and it flipped water all over the place. Other people pulled up and, when seeing the situation, simply drove away. I wasn't hassled or panhandled by any of these folks, but why can't this small park be made off limits to camping for sanitary reasons? Also a dog bowl like at Liberty Park would be a nice addition.

We need more trails, more use-specific trails and more trail maintenance so everyone can experience this incredible natural wonderland right in our own backyard. Hans Reichstetter

subject: more foothills trails
comment: Hi! It's my understanding that on August 27 there will be some consideration of re-funding/re-starting the trail-building process in the SLC foothills. This is my comment: I have been an avid user of the Salt Lake City foothills trails for the 25 years I've been in SLC, and was first exposed to them on a visit for the Outdoor Retailer show well before that, and that influenced my decision to move to UT. Proximity to hikeable/rideable trails is a very high priority for me - and, I think, for many people - and the foothills trails have been great....but are now outdated. Considering the proximity to so many other trail lovers there are too few trails in the very trail-friendly terrain and the ad hoc trails above and below the shoreline are basically overused game trails that are far from being "good" trails by today's standards. I was very excited to see the trails master plan unveiled several years ago at the Natural History Museum, was excited to see some of the trails being implemented, and was very disappointed to see the effort curtailed a couple of years ago. Trail design/development has come a long ways in the last 20 years, and the quality, popularity, and appropriate use of the designated trails is on ample display.....near, but not in Salt Lake City. Draper, Herriman, Lehi, Alpine, Park City, Moab, Eagle Mountain, Kamas, Hurricane, Richfield, Ogden, Provo, Logan, and others have been very progressive and have developed excellent networks that allow for easy mixed use with minimal conflicts, and Salt Lake City should follow suit. Appropriate hillside cutting, directional travel, and ped/horse/bike specific trails should be implemented, and will actually complement Salt Lake City's reputation as an "outdoor city"....that's based basically on the Wasatch, but not - yet - on the foothills. I understand that there are many demands on a city's infrastructure, but I firmly believe that trails very much enhances a city's liveability, and with increasing heat, pollution, lakebed dust, and increased crowding Salt Lake City needs more and better trails nearby. Please provide adequate funding and re-start the development process! Sincerely, Tom Diegel, Sugarhouse

subject: Improve Foothill trails

It is one of the best assets of living here. I was glad to hear that you are considering improvements. I strongly support improving and expanding the trail system with use-specific trails for a variety of abilities. Best, Julie Kiefer

subject: More trails
comment: SLC Council Please expand the trails system. It will be better for everyone in the community. Directional mountain bike trails like Park City trails are wonderful. Make them well designed and well built. Too many old trails are too steep and eroded. I'm a mountain bike coach and lead rides twice a week. The template has been built. Follow how Park City designs and builds trails. They are a world class leader in trail systems. Thanks Brent Flory MB1 Investments

subject: Better SLC Foothill Trails!
comment: Hello! My name is Maisie Stevens and I am a student at the University of Utah! I support more opportunities to enjoy nature and exercise without a long drive, so I love the idea of expanding foothills trails so close to my university! Thank you!

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: My family, friends, and I love riding the Foothill Trails. They're fun, have different levels, and are at a great location.This is where practice is held a lot of the time and we would love for there to be more trails soon! Thanks so much!

subject: Foothill Trails
comment: I am emailing in support of the release of city funding to improve and expand our foothill trails. My family uses the foothill trails weekly for biking and hiking and support the city investment in new trails and ongoing trail maintenance. Thank you! Melany

subject: Trails funding
comment: We run and mountain bike on the Bonneville Shoreline Trail several times a week and really value the ability to be outside in our amazing hills! We support city investment in new trails, trailheads, and ongoing trail maintenance. Thank you! Marian Florence Salt Lake City resident

subject: SLC foothills trail funding
comment: Thanks for considering this trails question. My family and I live in the 9th&9th neighborhood and use the foothill trail system from city creek to parleys canyon several times a week running and mountain biking. As the trails have improved it has been amazing seeing more families using them. Please keep supporting this healthy resource for our community. Nathan Florence

subject: Trails
comment: Dear Council Members, Please, please allow expansion of the Foothill trail systems. It's medicine for the soul and teaches our kids to respect the beautiful state they live in. With the growing population at the University, our trails are going to become more and more crowded. Park City and Draper hair figured out. Let's figure it out too!

subject: Foothills Trail System Plan
comment: The foothills around Salt Lake City are heavily used by hikers, bikers, runners, dog-walkers, and nature lovers. Without a workable, funded, and well managed plan, the foothills will continue to be loved to death. The time for a plan is overdue. I urge the city Council to move forward with this plan before the landscape is irreparably changed to the detriment of current and future residents. David E. Leta

subject: Additional funding for foothills trails
comment: I'm excited to see renewed funding for improved foothills trails around SLC for hiking, dog walking and directional trails for mountain biking. My family and I already enjoy the first phase trail and can't wait for more. Thanks for prioritizing outdoor recreation. - John

subject: Support for foothill trails
comment: Hello We are SLC residents and frequent trail users. We support investments in planned trails in the foothills so that the city can continue to support the growing outdoor community Thank you, Rachel Woods

subject: Support for Foothills Master Plan
comment: Hi City Council Members, I love this city and love the trails. Please vote yes to approve funding to continue work on the FH Master Plan. We continue to grow into a larger city and need more trails for all (bikers, runners, hikers, dog walkers, whatever). NICA also continues to grow in popularity so trails, parking, trailheads, and proper maintenance are important. Vote yes! Thanks - Jarrett Fisher (P.S. Tell Erin I say hi)

subject: Increase in our pay.
comment: You should not be getting a raise. It is up to you to decide how much??? Great if you let us decide how much we want to pay for things the city does. I would like to pay $0. If you get to say how much you want for a part time job with all you support staff you could reasonably need and that $52,000 + benefits and retirement a year is not enough. Why not release how much the total budget you guys make along with all staff and anything else including benefits and then let us vote on it?????? That would seem fair to most of us. We the people* get screwed by the government all the time and this is just one more example. -- Pati

subject: Opposed to new council salary raise
comment: Salt Lake City Council members: I strongly urge you to reject a new, higher salary raise for yourselves. I have witnessed, first-hand your conscientious and devoted attention to the city's business. Your service is appreciated and acknowledged. However, a new salary raise to $74,000 — on top of the one you just received weeks ago to $52,941 — is egregious. If approved, your salary would jump from $42,000 at the end of June, 2024 to $74,000. Please consider this: • The proposed increase comes as inflation and cost of living are causing hardships for your fellow Salt Lake residents and constituents. • With no checks and balances, you are exploiting your own authority to give yourself a raise. The optics look terrible. • Matched against other cities of comparable size (SLC population 209,593) with comparable features (airport, major university, major health care system, arts, corporate headquarters, etc.) SLC Council salaries would be double or triple what council colleagues in these compatible cities are making: o Boise $28,048. Capitol City (population 236,600) o Des Moines $35,000 Capitol City (population 210,381) o Tallahassee $45,000* Capitol City pending public ballot vote in November, 2024. (population 202,221) o Baton Rouge $37,049 Capitol City (population 219,573) • The Salt Lake City Council position is part-time. • According to ZipRecruiter (July, 2024) the average full time salary in Salt Lake City is $61,766. • The City Council is supported by a staff of 39 plus an Executive Director and each Council member is assigned a full-time constituent liaison. This is a veritable "army." Name another city in Utah that — percentage wise — has that level of support? This staff assists you with your work and costs the city $6.2 million. What was the council department budget just 6 years ago? $3.7 million. And what was the City Council salary that same year? $35,925. • The basis for your original raise is flawed. It's tied to the mayor's salary which automatically triggers your raise. Are there other municipalities that have this provision? It deserves closer public scrutiny. The mayor's new $212,000 salary (a $44,000 raise) is higher than what Utah Governor Spencer Cox makes at $165,600. Does the mayor of Salt Lake City have more responsibility than the governor of the state of Utah? • You already receive annual cost of living increases. • By what criteria is the raise being requested? Salt Lake City schools are closing. Families are leaving. The majority of Salt Lake City roads are in poor condition. Our parks are not well maintained. Police department morale is low. There have been some glaring RDA "fumbles." • Arguing on a local podcast that the current council salary is too low or too demanding timewise for some people triggers a "class warfare" narrative. Tell that to the countless number of Salt Lake retail wage earners or retail owners who gave their all and still lost their jobs, lost their businesses, lost their homes, lost employees, and everything else during COVID — while thousands of Salt Lake City employees were sheltered by the city's safe government harbor during COVID. Unless you have contrary evidence, not one Salt Lake City employee was laid off because of downsizing during COVID. Many worked from home. Additionally, the federal government dumped tens of millions of ARPA money into city government coffers. Do you understand the perception? During the toughest economic time in America your salary and the budget of this city ballooned. And now you want more. • The facts don't support your argument that a Council seat is primarily accessible to privileged, wealthy people. The current city council is the most diverse in the city's history – from many different aspects including work experience, ethnicity, and LGBTQ standards. Council salary has not prevented you or others from running and winning a council seat. • Every job has emergencies, overtime stresses, and unexpected demands. The city has faced several major issues recently requiring special attention and a great deal of time. Using the last 6 months as a yardstick for a salary increase may not be the best lens through which to see this issue clearly. • If your life has changed and you're in a different financial place then you were before you became a Council member, then maybe this job isn't for you anymore. It seems inappropriate that the go-too bailout solution should be hiking your Salt Lake City Council salary. What do other people do when faced with the same dilemma? Some have 2-3 jobs; some decide to move elsewhere; some leave the job they're in or cut back commitments; others re-educate themselves, change professions or jobs, get family assistance or something else. Thus far, a good case for a Council salary increase of this magnitude has not been made. What is your rationale? In the spirit of fairness and transparency the people of Salt Lake deserve to know. Respectfully, Janet (Jan) Hemming – Salt Lake resident

subject: Thoughts on SLC's Green Space Initiatives
comment: Dear Victoria, I'm a strong believer in investing in Salt Lake City's existing green spaces. The Jordan River is a scenic treasure winding through our valley, offering beautiful trails and natural areas. Unfortunately, years of neglect have created a negative perception of the Jordan River corridor. I'm excited about the upcoming developments along the trail, which I hope will revitalize this invaluable green space. While I appreciate the Mayor's vision for downtown green spaces, I believe we should prioritize investing in existing natural areas like the Jordan River. It seems more efficient to enhance what we already have rather than create new green spaces from scratch. I understand the Green Loop was a key campaign promise, and its approval may be inevitable. However, I felt it was important to share my perspective. I truly believe the Jordan River is an untapped gem that deserves our attention and investment. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Jeffrey Wood

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: I am calling cause my neighbors and myself, we have been looking at the Council newsletter and notice all things being done involve funding things. With the property taxes hitting a new all time highs every year, I think it would be good to do something about limiting taxes. Maybe cutting taxes a little bit. It is just too much. The growth in taxes and inflation in taxes is even more than food. I am calling on behalf of everyone and we are hoping you will consider things that will cut and lower taxes. Thank you so much.

subject: Support for Trails
comment: I may be racing a time out clock but I whole heartedly support increased trail access, development, and related funding efforts for SLC Foothill trails. My wife and I are SLC residents and we utilize existing trails regularly for ourselves, our dog, and with friends and family. Our utilization primarily comes from running and biking. I would love to see more trails of greater variety with greater connectivity across the Avenues neighborhood and BST corridor.

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: Hi my name is Anne Findlay. I am a resident of Salt Lake City and I am calling to express my support of the Foothills trails system improvements and to encourage the City Council to release funds to work on that. I think it is a really important part of Salt Lake City and it brings a lot of great opportunities to residents. It encourages being outside and being healthy. Anyway just wanted to share that, thanks bye.

subject: Motorized Bicycles
comment: Please consider keeping the foothills non-motorized (no batteries or electric MOTORS) these are creating a confrontational dynamic that was not present previous to their more recent popularity. There is a lot of danger on the trail because of the added capabilities of novice riders. Please keep motors off the foothills.

subject: Please do more to support our outdoor lifestyle
comment: So many of us live, work and spend time & money in SLC because of the great proximity to the outdoors that we love. With that said, Salt Lake City needs to do more to support its citizens in this passion. The trails are at capacity and there are regular conflicts. It is incredible to see the sheer number of folks using the trails in the mornings, evenings, and weekends. Salt Lake City lags far behind so many other cities that are benefiting from their investment in trails including Draper, Lehi, Herriman, Spanish Fork, North Salt Lake and Bountiful. Mountain Biking continues to grow and incredible rates and isn't expected to slow. I am writing to voice my support for the Foothills Master Plan. The newly completed trails in the Foothills are fantastic, and I'd love to see phase 1 completed and phase 2 begun on schedule. Please don't be persuaded by the vocal few who would put a stop to the mountain bikers who love to spend time in the outdoors. Just spend a few hours on the trails on a weekend morning and see the joy these trails bring to so many and the return the investment is already seeing. Thank you, Brian Carter

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: Good morning, I missed the cut-off time for submitting an email regarding this evening's vote on the foothill plan. I will read my email..... I understand the council has taken another look at funding for trails after hitting the pause button for serval years. Thank you for judicially considering concerns and please move forward with expanding and rehabilitating current offerings. Our foothills are a precious commodity that deserves the attention that our neighbors to the north and south have invested in. Thank you very much, Scott Marshal.

subject: foothills trails plan
comment: Dear SLC City Council members; Over the last 10 years or so greatly increased use of the existing foothills trails above SLC has caused environmental damage, crowding and situations of mixed user conflict. To deal with these problems Salt Lake City dearly needs expanded and improved trails in the SLC foothills. In planning since 2016, the Foothills Trails Plan began construction in 2020 of much needed new trails to provide family friendly and user specific trails. Unfortunately this phase of trail work was halted in 2021. Since then SLC Public Lands Department has undertaken a thorough reevaluation of the Foothills Trails Plan and is ready to begin trails work with a new focus on sustainable and effective trail design and construction. As an avid and frequent user of the foothills trails - both as a hiker and mountain biker - I strongly encourage the City Council to approve the request by SLC Public Lands to release funding so they can continue to implement the Foothills Plan and provide new and improved trails for our active city residents. Thank you; Kenton Peters

subject: SLC Foothills Trails System: Note of Support
comment: Hi, I'm glad to hear that the SLC Council is re-prioritizing trails funding after the few-year pause. We need the improvements/expansions to our existing trails are badly needed to support the increased access and use. I regularly use these trails and would love to see them expanded and better designed. Thank you! Ethan

subject: Foothill Trails System improvements
comment: I ride and hike the foothill trails weekly. Please release funding to continue development of the trail systems.

subject: Living Room Trail "Renovation" Project
comment: Hello, Darin: I just learned about a large Living Room "renovation" project that sought NO public input before accessing taxpayer money to pay a private company without a bidding process. I understand that neither the Mayor's office nor the City Council knew about this massive project beforehand, despite a pledge by Public Lands in February 2024 to provide transparency and inclusivity in the planning and implementation of trail improvement projects. Instead, Public Lands has engaged with Trails Utah on this project covertly and in secret since autumn 2023, wholly undermining their so-called commitment to transparency and inclusivity. They stated they would follow the SE Group recommendations to work with community stakeholders and obtain scientific and user data BEFORE implementing any Foothills trails projects. Public Lands has not. I also understand that the changes Trails Utah plans to make, which includes blasting bedrock, are substantial enough to be considered construction and not merely "renovation." Further, trails in George's Hollow are slated for construction under this project name. No one asked for these changes. Why are public funds being offered up without public knowledge and input? Knowing these facts, how can anyone have faith in Public Lands and their leadership? We should oppose this project both on the merits and on principle. Public Lands must follow their stated commitments of transparency and inclusivity when planning projects involving taxpayer money on our public lands. Public Lands officials involved in this Living Room "renovation" project need to explain themselves. Why are they lying to the public and engaging in shady deals that will significantly alter our most beloved Foothill trails? Please help us to immediately halt this massive and unwarranted construction project. Thank you. Best, Diane Walker

subject: More SLC Foothill Trails now!
comment: As a resident of Salt Lake County who so often uses Foothill Trails for walking my dog, mountain biking, hiking, etc. I am thrilled to hear that the SLC Council is re-prioritizing funding for the trails after a 3-year pause. I strongly support moving forward to build and improve foothill trails with the additional considerations.

subject: We love our SLC Foothills Trails and Want More of Them
comment: Hello - I live in Federal Heights and we are frequent (almost daily) users of our trails. I was very excited when we started adding more trails to spread us out and let everyone make use of this wonderful resource we have. And I was very disappointed when we decided to stop building them a few years ago. These trails are a wonderful resource for our community and people of all income levels and I believe they make us healthier and happier and improve everything about living here. Please start building new trails again and making this one of the greatest cities in the world. Thank you, Ann Brisk

subject: Open Trails
comment: As a long-time resident of Salt Lake City, I want to commend the city on the improvements that have been made to the Foothill Trails over the years. I remember when Dry Creek was connected to Citycreek and support having a planned trail system for current and future generations to enjoy. Sincerely, Matthew Smith

subject: Foothill trails
comment: I use the foothill trails 5 days a week. I'd love funding and support of the trails and additional trails! Thanks for the consideration on the vote tonight David.

subject: Foothill Trails System Improvements
comment: Hello, our family members are avid users of the local trail system in Salt Lake City and would love to see funding allocated towards improvements for these trails. Many in our neighborhood in Salt Lake also use the trails and would support this for sure. Thanks for your consideration. -Gary Moore Dearborn Street, SLC, UT

subject: Sports complex meeting on 8/27
comment: Dear Mr. Mano, As a SLC resident for 25 years who is married to a resident of 50 years, I (and my husband) are strongly opposed to the entire sports complex proposal. We loathe the idea of the downtown centerpiece being a sports arena (especially an ice hockey arena, Who cares about ice hockey??). But especially egregious is that the public was not given an opportunity to weigh in on this decision, AND we are expected to pay for it! Our property taxes are already high, all our utilities are rising exponentially, and now we have to pay for a giant boondoggle that we don't want at all? This is a wasted opportunity to revitalize downtown with a strong pedestrian-only core, like so many vibrant European cities have, full of independent shops and outdoor cafes/restaurants, and reachable by convenient and inexpensive public transit. The money raised for this "revitalization" effort could do so, so, so much more good spent on transport, air quality measures, supporting small businesses, and affordable housing. Thank you for your attention. Margie McCloy

subject: Proposed Sports Complex and increased taxes
comment: I am a senior on a fixed income living in Rose Park, and I am increasingly concerned and frustrated with rising costs in all aspects of living here. I don't know how much longer I can afford to live in Utah, in general, and in Salt Lake City, specifically, due to the rapid increases in utilities, property taxes and housing costs in general, and sales taxes. That leads me to the reason for this email: I am adamantly opposed to the proposed .5% sales tax increase that is ONLY going to be assessed in Salt Lake City. People from surrounding suburbs and counties—especially Davis, Utah, Summit, and Tooele—commute to work in Salt Lake County, and undoubtedly will attend some of the events this venue will provide. I believe they should also help pay for this construction/redevelopment. If more counties/suburbs were included in this taxation, the rate could be substantially lowered, since it seems obvious this subsidy of the Smith Entertainment Group will be approved. I actually think the attendees of these events could fund it through special assessments on the ticket sales and parking fees; that way, those who actually want this venue have a vested interest in it. I have zero interest in hockey or basketball and resent being asked for pay a great sum of money for it over the proposed 30-year tax increase. I hope you will actually consider the dissenting opinions that come in to your office. I would like to see this come up for a referendum, rather than having this forced on us. Sincerely, Nancy Coffeen

subject: Foothills Trail System improvements
comment: I want to voice my support for prioritizing trail funding to build and improve foothill trails in the Salt Lake City area. I'm an avid trail user, along with the Highland High School mtb team I help to coach and the many other SLC high school teams. Crowding is becoming an issue, and many of the older trails are too steep or suffering from erosion. I'd also like to see more "directional" trails arranged for the multi-purpose users to minimize conflict. Thanks, Ken

subject: New sports complex downtown
comment: From what I've read and heard, I believe it's useless to protest the new hockey team. It's deeply disappointing to live in a city that values sports at the expense of art. If I must help finance a billionaire's pet project, I can only hope that this inevitable monstrosity raises my property value so I can get a better price when I finally GTFO of toxic lake city.

subject: Please vote against sports complex tax to SLC residents
comment: Councilmember Mano, Please vote against any additional taxing the SLC residents to assist the Smiths with building their sports complex. The increase in all of our city bills & utility bills are already more than the residents of SLC and your district are able to pay for. All of them have doubled or tripled in price in less than 2 years but our service has declined in all areas. These increases to residents like me who invested large amounts of money in upgrading my heating and ac system this summer. I also rarely watered my lawn, only my trees. For the first time in almost 20 years I purposely did not plant a garden or flowers to avoid a spike in my utilities, but it seems there is nothing we can do to stabilize our costs in any way. Please think of the additional hardship this tax will put on the residents of this city and please represent the residents of your district. The Smiths were able to functionally purchase the property in Sandy without an increased burden on Sandy taxpayers and SLC as a much larger city should be able to do the same. Thank you, Harmony McQueen

subject: Foothills trails
comment: I am a proponent of releasing funds for trail expansion in the SLC foothills...however, feel that ALL e-bikes should not be allowed. If it has a motor (ie electric motor), it IS a motorized vehicle, regardless of whether it has a throttle or not. Unfortunately, in many areas of Utah, folks ride faster than is safe, and put others at risk. E-bikes should ONLY be allowed on wide, paved trails.

subject: Please restart the Foothills Trail program
comment: I'm a 64 year older hiker and mountain biker that really enjoys using the new trails built a few years ago. I would love to see the trail building start up again, especially in regions located above the BST elevation. The Meridian area has tons of potential to get trail users more dispersed. Good progress has been made on improving trailhead. Please make sure that trailhead improvements include increasing parking capacity. Popperton looks like it is going to be great. Thank you, James Hicks
